label: Heaven over Heaven
general: Something wants to begin, and you have the power to begin it. This hexagram is made entirely of solid lines, pure creative energy with nothing holding it back, like the sky moving through its endless cycle of days. It's rare to feel this much momentum, and it's a real gift. But energy alone isn't the point. What turns raw power into something lasting is persistence: showing up again and again, staying aligned with what's right, not burning out in one bright flare. The risk here is arrogance, mistaking strength for permission to push everyone aside, or charging so far ahead that you lose touch with the ground. Use this time to start what matters, set a direction you can sustain, and keep renewing your effort. Strength that keeps going is worth far more than strength that shows off.
judgment: Pure creative force, the origin everything else moves out from. This is power at its most complete, and it works through you when you meet it with persistence rather than force. Stay with it, keep going, and it carries all the way to success. The energy is already here; the discipline to sustain it is what the moment asks.
image: Heaven moves, and never stops moving, day into night into day without tiring. Meet your own work the same way: keep yourself strong, renew your effort, and don't mistake rest for arrival.
lineTexts: The dragon lies hidden in the deep water. The power is real, but this isn't its moment yet. Don't act on it now. Let your strength gather out of sight, and trust that staying hidden at this stage is part of the work, not a failure to begin.

The dragon appears in the field, out in the open for the first time. Your ability is starting to show, and it's a good moment to seek out someone wiser or more established who can recognize it and help it grow. Being seen early is a gift; use it to learn.

You're active all day and still watchful in the evening, working hard and never quite at ease. The position is genuinely risky, and that alertness is exactly what keeps you safe. Stay careful and steady, and no mistake will follow.

The dragon seems ready to leap, yet it still rests in the deep. You're at a threshold: free to rise or to hold back, with no one forcing the choice. Weigh it honestly. Whichever you choose, if you choose with clear eyes, there's no blame in it.

The dragon flies in the open sky, at the height of its power and fully in its element. This is the moment of greatest influence, and it's good to connect with others of real stature. Use the height well: what you do from here reaches far.

The dragon has flown too high, past its proper limits. Strength that never rests turns into arrogance, and arrogance loses touch with everyone below. There will be regret here. Notice where you've pushed too far, and come back down before the fall does it for you.
beneficial: Strong creative momentum; a good time to begin what truly matters.
beware: Power without persistence burns out; don't let strength turn into arrogance.
allChanging: When every line changes, you see a whole host of dragons, none of them taking the lead. Pure strength has learned to yield: no one insists on being the head, and power moves without arrogance. That's good fortune. The creative force is at its best when it no longer needs to dominate.
reflections: What is yours to start here?
How could you keep going, not just start strong?
Where might your strength push others aside?

label: Earth over Earth
general: This is a time to receive rather than to lead. Every line in this hexagram is open, like the earth: wide, patient, ready to carry whatever is placed on it. That's not weakness. It takes real strength to support, follow, and let something grow through you instead of from you. The situation already has a direction; your task is to sense it and work with it. If you try to take the lead, set the agenda, or force an outcome, you'll lose your way. If you listen, follow good guidance, and give steady, devoted effort, you'll find yourself exactly where you need to be. Look for the people and conditions that can carry you forward. Being receptive now isn't passivity. It's trusting the ground under your feet.
judgment: A different kind of strength: the power to yield, receive, and carry. Success here doesn't come from leading the way but from following it, letting the ground of the situation guide you instead of forcing your own direction. Be steady and devoted, strong the way a good horse is strong, willing rather than driven, and you'll find your footing. Try to lead from the front now and you lose your way.
image: The earth takes whatever is laid on it and holds it all without complaint. Let your character have that kind of breadth: carry people and circumstances with a generous, unforced strength.
lineTexts: You feel hoarfrost under your feet. It's only a thin layer now, but it tells you that solid ice is coming. Small signs point to larger things. Notice where something is quietly beginning to set, for better or worse, and respond while it's still easy.

Straight, square and great, like the earth itself. You don't need to strain or plan every move here; acting honestly and naturally, true to your nature, is enough. Without repeated effort, everything turns out well. This is receptive strength at its best.

You keep your gifts quietly under restraint while staying true to them. If you work in someone else's service, don't claim the credit for yourself. Do the work well, let others take the stage, and you will bring things to a good end. Hidden excellence still counts.

A sack tied shut. This is a time to keep your own counsel, saying little and holding back. Discretion brings neither blame nor praise. When the situation is uncertain or risky, staying closed and quiet protects you, even if no one notices what you held back.

The yellow lower garment, a sign of quiet dignity and modesty. Yellow was the color of the earth and the center, and the lower garment was worn humbly beneath. Real worth that doesn't need to display itself brings great good fortune.

Dragons fight in the open field, and their blood is dark and yellow. The yielding force has pushed too far and now clashes with the strong one, and both are wounded. When receptivity tries to seize power instead of supporting it, the struggle hurts everyone.
beneficial: Support, receptivity and steady effort will carry you where you need to go.
beware: Trying to lead or force the outcome now will make you lose your way.
allChanging: When every line changes, the receptive becomes strong. What matters now is lasting steadiness: stay firm, correct and true over the long run, and advantage will come. Yielding has found its backbone. Gentleness that endures is a quiet but real power.
reflections: Which way is this already moving?
Whose guidance is worth following here?
Where could listening help more than steering?

label: Water over Thunder
general: Something new is genuinely beginning, and it's hard in the way that only real beginnings are. Picture a seed that has cracked open underground but hasn't yet broken the surface. There's life in it, real momentum, but it's pushing through dense, tangled ground, and from the outside nothing looks finished or even certain. That's the moment you're in. The difficulty you feel isn't a sign you've chosen wrong; it's the friction of growth itself. The mistake here is impatience, forcing the shoot up before it's ready, or reading the struggle as failure and pulling back. What this asks of you instead is steadiness. Don't try to do it alone, and don't rush to lock in a direction. Gather people who can support you, hold to your sense of purpose, and let the first true shape of the thing emerge before you commit to where it's going.
judgment: A time of real promise, but the promise is still buried in difficulty, and only patience brings it through. Don't strike out toward some far-off goal yet. What helps now isn't bold action, it's the right support around you. Find the people who can steady the work, and stay the course instead of chasing a quick resolution.
image: Thunder stirs below and clouds gather above: energy and confusion in the same sky, not yet broken into rain. Meet a tangled beginning by bringing order to it patiently, sorting the threads and giving the chaos a shape, rather than waiting for it to clear on its own.
lineTexts: You meet an obstacle almost at once and feel the pull to force your way past it. Hold still instead and stay true to your purpose. This is the moment to set solid foundations and bring in people who can help, not to charge ahead alone.

The difficulties stack up and progress stalls; the horses seem to pull the cart backward. The old image is a young woman who turns down a suitor who isn't right, and waits ten years for the right union. Don't accept a commitment that isn't right yet. What isn't ready now can still come right in its own time.

Chasing the goal without a guide is like hunting deer in the forest with no forester to show the way; you'll only lose yourself among the trees. Read the moment honestly. Knowing when to stop isn't weakness here; it's wisdom. Pushing on now leads to regret.

Again the horses pull back and the way looks blocked, but this time reaching out is right. Set aside pride and move toward the help or the connection you need, from someone who genuinely wants to join with you. Taking that step now brings good fortune.

You have real good to give, but it isn't flowing freely to others yet. In small, steady measures your efforts land and do good. Trying to force large change all at once will go badly. Work at the scale the moment allows.

The horses turn back, and tears of blood flow. Here the struggle reaches its hardest point, where the effort collapses and grief follows. It names the real cost of pushing a beginning past what it can bear. Grieve, stop, and let yourself begin again differently.
beneficial: Something real is taking root; the difficulty is a sign of genuine growth.
beware: Rushing can snap the shoot before it's strong.
reflections: What are you rushing that needs more time?
Who could help you through this start?
What if the struggle is a sign of growth?

label: Mountain over Water
general: You're at the start of learning something, and you don't yet know what you don't know. That's not a problem; it's simply where wisdom begins. Picture a spring at the foot of a mountain, water just emerging, not sure which way it will flow. The question is how you learn. Real guidance comes when you seek it out sincerely, not when you wait for it to be handed to you. Ask clearly, once, and listen. If you keep asking the same question until you hear the answer you want, you're no longer learning, you're bargaining. This applies to the I Ching itself: casting again because you didn't like the result shows you weren't ready to hear it. Be humble, be patient with your own inexperience, and let each lesson settle before you rush to the next.
judgment: Inexperience, the not-yet-knowing of someone at the start of learning. There's success in it, but on one condition: the learner comes to the teacher, not the reverse, and comes sincerely. Ask once, with real attention, and you receive an answer. Pester for a different one and you've stopped listening; nothing more will come. Trust the first response and stay with it.
image: A spring wells up at the foot of the mountain, water just beginning its course, not yet knowing which way it will run. Grow the way water finds its channel: through steady, thorough persistence, doing each thing properly until the path makes itself clear.
lineTexts: Breaking through ignorance takes some discipline at first; the shackles have to come off. A firm hand can help someone wake up. But keep it short. If the strictness becomes a habit, it turns into its own kind of chain, and that will bring regret.

Be patient with people who don't know yet, and stay open to learning even from those others overlook. That generosity brings good fortune. The image is a young person ready to take responsibility for the household: maturity shows in how kindly you treat inexperience.

The traditional text warns against marrying someone who loses themselves the moment they see wealth. The lesson is for anyone: don't throw yourself at whatever glitters, and don't bind yourself to someone who would. Grasping at the first impressive thing you see brings no advantage.

You're stuck in your own ignorance, tangled in it, and too far from anyone who could help. Clinging to your current view will only bring regret. Notice how isolated your thinking has become, and look for a way to let someone or something new reach you.

The simple openness of someone young and inexperienced, willing to be taught. This is beginner's mind at its best: no pretense, no defensiveness, just readiness to learn. That humility brings good fortune. Approach your situation as a student, not as an expert.

Ignorance is being punished, struck hard. Harshness that injures does no good. What helps is protecting someone from harm, guarding against the real dangers, rather than punishing them. Correct mistakes in a way that shields people, including yourself, instead of wounding them.
beneficial: An honest beginner's mind; sincere questions will bring real guidance.
beware: Asking until you hear what you want means you've stopped listening.
reflections: What don't you know yet?
Who could teach you?
Which answer are you hoping to hear?

label: Water over Heaven
general: What you need is coming, but not yet. Clouds have gathered; the rain hasn't fallen. The pull is to act anyway, to force the moment, or to fill the waiting with worry. Neither helps. This hexagram asks for confident waiting: knowing that the situation is moving toward resolution even when you can't see progress. That kind of patience isn't passive. It's an inner strength that comes from trusting yourself and your timing. Use the waiting well. Rest, eat, keep your spirits up, look after what sustains you, so that when the moment arrives you're ready rather than exhausted. Danger may be near, but it's no reason to panic. Stay calm, stay sincere about what you want, and when the time is right, you'll be able to move decisively and well.
judgment: Waiting, but not the idle kind. The strength is already gathered in you; what's missing is the right moment, and it hasn't arrived. Hold your position with genuine confidence rather than anxiety, and the waiting itself becomes the success. When the time is ripe, even the great crossing ahead will be favorable.
image: Clouds have climbed into the sky and hang there full, before any rain falls. While you wait, eat well, rest, keep your spirits up: nourish yourself so you're ready, instead of wearing yourself down with worry.
lineTexts: You're waiting out in the meadow, far from the danger. Nothing has happened yet, and you're tempted to rush toward it. Don't. Stay with your ordinary life, keep your steadiness, and you won't go wrong. The waiting here is calm, and it should stay that way.
You're waiting on the sand, closer to the river now. There may be some talk, a little criticism or gossip. Let it pass without reacting. Stay calm and patient, and in the end things turn out well.

You're waiting in the mud at the water's edge. You moved too close too soon, and now you're exposed; your own impatience invites trouble. Be very careful from here. Recognize how you got into this position, and don't make it worse.

You're waiting in blood, in the middle of the danger itself. This is serious, but there's a way out of the pit. Don't struggle wildly. Stay calm, let things take their course, and you can get yourself free.

Waiting at a table with food and wine. In the middle of the waiting there's a pause, a moment of ease. Enjoy it, rest and gather strength, but keep your purpose steady. Use the calm to stay ready, and good fortune follows.

You've fallen into the pit, and the waiting seems to be over in the worst way. Then three unexpected guests arrive. Help may come from where you least expect it. Receive them with respect, even if they're not who you hoped for, and it ends in good fortune.
beneficial: What you need is on its way; rest and prepare while you wait.
beware: Worry and forcing the timing will drain the strength you'll soon need.
reflections: What exactly are you waiting for?
How can you look after yourself while you wait?
Which worries are draining your strength?

label: Heaven over Water
general: There's a conflict, and you may well be right. But being right isn't the same as winning, and pushing the dispute to the bitter end will cost you more than it gains. Heaven pulls upward, water sinks down, and the two keep moving apart; that's the nature of this situation. The wise move is to stop halfway: state your case, then look for a fair resolution instead of total victory. Bring in someone impartial if you need to. This is not the time to start a risky new venture while the conflict is still alive, because you'd be building on unstable ground. Above all, look at how this began. Most conflicts can be prevented by getting things clear at the start. If you can't prevent this one, at least keep it from hardening into something permanent.
judgment: You're in the right, and still you're being blocked. That's the shape of conflict here. Stopping halfway, before it hardens into a fight to the finish, brings good fortune; pushing all the way through to win brings the opposite. Look for a fair, respected authority to hear it out. This is not the moment to launch a risky venture.
image: Heaven rises and water sinks, two forces moving steadily apart. Where things naturally pull in opposite directions, head off the conflict before it starts: get the terms clear at the very beginning, while it's still easy.
lineTexts: The conflict is only beginning. Let it drop rather than drag it out. You may hear some criticism, but walking away from a fight early costs very little. In the end, things will turn out well.

You can't win this one, so you withdraw to a small, quiet place, like retreating to a village of three hundred households. That isn't defeat; it's wisdom. Stepping back from a battle you can't win protects you and the people around you. No blame.

You live on what you've already earned and keep to your old place. It feels exposed and risky, but holding steady brings good fortune in the end. If you serve someone else's cause, don't chase the credit. Quiet loyalty outlasts the fight.

You can't win this, so you turn back, accept the situation, and change your attitude toward it. That isn't giving up; it's returning to what's right and letting go of the need to prevail. Settling into steadiness instead of pressing the conflict brings good fortune.

The dispute is brought before someone fair and wise. When a conflict reaches a just and impartial judge, it can be settled for good. If you're in the right, this is the place to make your case. Great good fortune.

You win the dispute and are rewarded with a leather belt of honor. But the old text says it's taken away three times before the morning ends. A victory won by fighting to the end never stays won. You'll have to keep defending it.
beneficial: A fair resolution is possible if you stop before the fight hardens.
beware: Pushing to win at all costs will cost more than it gains.
reflections: What would a fair outcome look like?
When would this fight cost more than it's worth?
What could have been clearer from the start?

label: Earth over Water
general: This situation needs many people working as one. It might be a team, a family, a community, or the many parts of yourself pulling in different directions. Like water collected beneath the earth, the strength is there, but it needs to be organized. That only works with good leadership: someone experienced, trusted, and committed to the common good rather than their own glory. If that's you, lead with discipline and fairness. If it isn't, support the right person. Shared effort without direction scatters; direction without care for the people involved turns harsh. Be clear about the goal, steady in purpose, and generous with the people who carry the load. Strength built this way runs deep, quiet and lasting, without needing to be shown off.
judgment: A situation that calls for organized effort, many parts moving as one. That only works with a leader who is experienced and trusted, and with the discipline to persevere. Put the right person at the center, hold to a steady course, and this brings good fortune with no blame.
image: Water gathers hidden within the earth, a whole reservoir held out of sight below the surface. Build your strength the same quiet way: draw people to you through generosity and care, and your reserves deepen without display.
lineTexts: The army sets out, and it has to go in good order. A shared effort only works if it starts with clear purpose and discipline. If it begins badly, it will end badly. Get the foundations right before you march.

You're in the middle of the army, the trusted leader the effort depends on. Good fortune and no blame. Those above you show their full trust, again and again. Lead from among your people, not from far above them.

The army may return carrying its dead. When too many people try to lead, or the wrong person takes charge, the effort fails. Divided command brings disaster. Make sure it's clear who is actually leading.

The army retreats. That's no mistake. When the odds are against you, pulling back in good order is the wise move, and it keeps your strength intact for later. Knowing when to withdraw, without shame or panic, is part of leading well.

There's game in the field, a real threat to deal with, and it's right to act. Put the experienced leader in charge. If younger, less capable people take over the command, the effort will fail, however well-intentioned it is.

The great ruler hands out rewards and positions when the work is done. Give responsibility to those who earned it by character, not just by success. People of small character shouldn't be put in charge, however useful they were in the campaign.
beneficial: Organized, shared effort under good leadership can achieve a great deal.
beware: Effort without direction scatters; direction without care turns harsh.
reflections: What needs to pull in one direction here?
Who is best placed to lead this?
What shared goal could bring order to the effort?

label: Water over Earth
general: This is about coming together, finding where you belong and who you belong with. Water on the earth flows into every hollow until it becomes one body. Something similar is possible for you now: a bond, a group, a partnership, a shared commitment. Before you join, check yourself honestly. Do you have the steadiness this union will need? Are you joining for the right reasons? If you're the center others are gathering around, ask whether you can carry that responsibility. Union brings good fortune, but timing matters. Hesitate too long and the moment passes, the circle closes without you. Reach out, commit sincerely, and keep good relations with those around you. Real belonging is built, not waited for.
judgment: Coming together, forming real bonds around a shared center. There's good fortune in it. First be honest with yourself about what you bring to the union, whether you have the steadiness and staying power it asks for. Those still unsure can gradually join, and are welcome. But don't wait too long: come too late and the moment for joining has passed.
image: Water rests on the earth, flowing into every hollow until it all joins as one body. Draw close in that spirit: build genuine ties and keep good relations with the people around you, rather than standing apart.
lineTexts: Join with others sincerely, right from the start. Let your honesty be full, like a plain earthen jar filled to the brim: nothing fancy, just real. Union built on that kind of sincerity attracts good fortune over time, sometimes from places you never expected.

This connection comes from within, from genuine feeling rather than calculation or need. It's union rooted in your own center. Stay true to yourself while you draw close to others, and don't give yourself away to be accepted. Holding that line brings good fortune.

You're seeking to join with the wrong people. Not everyone who offers closeness is someone you should be bound to, and some bonds pull you away from who you are. Look honestly at who you're aligning with, and why, before you commit any further.

You reach outward to join someone of real worth, beyond your usual circle. It may feel like a step up or a step away from the familiar. Doing it openly and steadily, with good intentions, brings good fortune. Union with good leadership strengthens you.

The model of true union is the old king who drives the game from three sides only and lets the animals escape through the fourth. He doesn't force anyone to stay. People join him freely, without being warned or pushed. Openness like that draws others in, and brings good fortune.

Seeking union without ever having made a real beginning, like a group with no head. The chance to belong has passed, or was never truly taken. If you hesitated too long, or never committed at all, the circle has closed. This brings misfortune, and the lesson is about timing.
beneficial: Real belonging is within reach; reach out and commit sincerely.
beware: Wait too long, or join for the wrong reasons, and the moment passes.
reflections: Who or what are you drawn to join?
What would this commitment ask of you?
What might you lose by waiting too long?

label: Wind over Heaven

names.wilhelm: The Taming Power of the Small

general: You're being held back by something small, and it's frustrating. Dense clouds without rain: the pressure builds, but the release doesn't come. Here, the gentle force of wind is briefly holding back the strength of heaven. This isn't the moment for a big breakthrough. Your influence right now is limited, so use it where it actually works: in small, patient, consistent steps. Refine your plans, take care of details, build trust gradually. Forcing the large outcome now will only waste your energy. This hexagram is about accumulating, slowly gathering what you'll need later. The rain will come. In the meantime, let gentleness be your strength, and trust that small things done well are quietly preparing the ground.
judgment: Something small is holding back something large, the way a light wind can only briefly check the sky's great energy. Success is coming, but not yet in full. Dense clouds have gathered and no rain has fallen; the pressure is building without release. Work with what little influence you genuinely have right now, patiently, instead of forcing the big result before its time.
image: The wind moves across the face of heaven, shaping the clouds without stopping them. When you can't change the large thing yet, refine the small ones: polish your character and your conduct in the details, and let that gentle, steady influence be your power for now.
lineTexts: You return to your own path. How could that be a mistake? When something small holds you back, going back to what you know is right, instead of pushing against the obstacle, is the best response. There's no blame in turning around. Good fortune.

You're drawn back to the right path, pulled along by others who are returning too. You don't have to find the way alone; going with them is wise. Letting good company steady your direction brings good fortune.

The spokes have burst from the wagon wheel, and the cart can't move. The old image is a husband and wife who can't look each other in the eye. Something small has turned into open friction. Forcing your way forward now will only break things further.

You stay sincere, and the danger passes. Blood is avoided and fear gives way. Honesty and good faith can keep a tense situation from turning into a real fight, even when you're the weaker party. Hold to that sincerity, and no blame follows.

You're sincere and loyally connected to others, and they to you. That bond makes you rich, not on your own but through your neighbors. Shared good faith multiplies what each of you has. What you couldn't hold back alone, you can hold together.

The rain has finally come, and things settle. What could be gathered has been gathered. Now isn't the time to press further. The old text compares it to the moon when it's nearly full: one more push tips into decline. Rest in what's been achieved, and don't force the next step.
beneficial: Small, patient steps are quietly building toward something larger.
beware: Forcing the big result now only wastes your energy.
reflections: What small step can you take now?
Which details could you work on meanwhile?
What are you slowly building toward?

label: Heaven over Lake
general: You're in a delicate situation, perhaps dealing with someone more powerful than you, or moving through territory where one wrong step has consequences. The old image is treading on the tail of a tiger, and yet the tiger doesn't bite. Why? Because of how you walk: with care, courtesy, and awareness of where you stand. This hexagram is about conduct. Know your position and act accordingly, not with fear, but with clear-eyed respect for the situation. Don't be careless or arrogant, and don't freeze either. Move forward step by step, mindful of the people and the power around you. Done this way, even a risky path can be walked safely. Good conduct isn't timidity; it's what makes it possible to go where others can't.
judgment: You're walking a risky path, close enough to the danger to feel it, like treading on a tiger's tail. Yet handled with the right care and courtesy, the tiger doesn't bite, and you come through. It's not recklessness that saves you here but a steady, respectful alertness to exactly where you're placing each step.
image: Heaven stands above, the lake lies below, each in its proper place, the order unmistakable. Tread your own path the same way: know where you stand, treat people according to what's right, and let that clarity steady your footing through the danger.
lineTexts: You walk your accustomed path simply, without ambition or pretense. You're not trying to impress anyone or climb anywhere yet. Going forward this way brings no blame. Straightforward conduct, free of hidden agendas, is a strong place to begin any risky journey.

You walk a level, smooth path, quiet and on your own, without needing anyone's approval or attention. You're not caught up in the competition around you. Staying steady and true like this, you move safely, and good fortune follows. Not everyone needs to follow the crowd.

The one-eyed man thinks he can see, the lame man thinks he can walk, and he treads on the tiger's tail and is bitten. Overestimating yourself in a dangerous place brings misfortune. It's the image of someone playing a role far bigger than they can carry. Know your limits honestly.

You tread on the tiger's tail, and you know exactly where you are. Full of caution, you keep your wits about you and move with great care. That alertness, far from being weakness, is what carries you through. In the end, there's good fortune.

You walk resolutely, sure of yourself and your course, perhaps with the authority to act as you see fit. Even when you're right, there's real danger in being too certain and too fixed. Stay firm in what you know, but stay awake to the risk.

Look back over the path you've walked and examine where it has led you. Your conduct over time is the truest sign of what's coming. If the whole course has been sound, if you've walked it with care, great good fortune follows.
beneficial: Careful, courteous conduct lets you walk safely where others can't.
beware: On this path, one careless or arrogant step has real consequences.
reflections: Where do you need to tread carefully?
How could courtesy help you here?
What does your conduct show others?

label: Earth over Heaven
general: This is a good time. Heaven and earth are in contact, and everything flows. Communication opens up, people cooperate, plans come together, and small difficulties give way to larger good. Enjoy it, and make use of it. Times like this are when foundations get built, relationships deepen, and long-delayed projects move. Don't coast, though. Peace is easier to keep when you actively tend it: share what's good, help others benefit from the flow, and shape the conditions so this harmony can last as long as possible. Remember too that every season turns. The point isn't to fear the change that will eventually come, but to use the good time well, so you're stronger and better connected when it does.
judgment: A time of genuine flourishing, when heaven and earth are in contact and everything communicates freely. The small and petty recede, the great and generous come forward. Good fortune, and success that flows. This is the good season, the opening you've been waiting for; move with it while it's here.
image: Heaven and earth draw together and mingle, and from their meeting all things thrive. In a time this favorable, help it along: shape the conditions so the good can circulate, and guide people toward it, rather than standing back and letting the moment coast.
lineTexts: When you pull up one blade of grass, others come with it, because their roots are joined. In a good time, people rise together, and one person's progress lifts those connected to them. Move forward alongside the people who share your purpose. Good fortune.

Be generous with people who are rough or unrefined, bold enough to cross the river without a boat, mindful of what's far away, and free of narrow factions. That's how to walk the middle way in a time of peace: inclusive, brave, and fair.

No plain without a slope, no going without a return. Good times shift, and difficulty will come back around. Stay steady and true when it does, and don't grieve over it. There's still good fortune to enjoy in what you have now.

You come down from your position to meet others, not boasting of your wealth, simply joining your neighbors in good faith. No warning or pressure is needed; people trust each other sincerely and come together freely. In a time of peace, openness flows naturally.

The old story tells of a king who gave his sister in marriage to a man of lower rank, and she took her place modestly. The lesson is about humility from those in high positions: when those above reach down to those below as equals, it brings blessing and great good fortune.

The city wall crumbles back into the moat it was built from. The time of peace is coming to an end. Don't use force to fight it. Speak only to those closest to you. Even if you're in the right, trying to hold on here will bring regret.
beneficial: Things flow and people cooperate; enjoy this good season and build on it.
beware: Good times turn; don't coast, tend the harmony while it lasts.
reflections: What is going well right now?
Who could share in this good time?
What could you build while things are easy?

label: Heaven over Earth
general: Things are stuck. Heaven and earth have pulled apart, communication breaks down, and the wrong people seem to be gaining ground while good intentions go nowhere. It's not your fault, and you can't fix it by force. This is a time to protect your integrity rather than push for results. Don't compromise yourself to get ahead, and don't be tempted by rewards that would require you to give up what you value. Draw back, keep your own counsel, and wait. Standstill doesn't last forever; every extreme eventually turns into its opposite. What matters now is coming through it intact, with your values whole, so you're ready to act when the way opens again.
judgment: The opposite season: heaven and earth turn away from each other and nothing gets through. Communication stalls, the small and petty rise while the great withdraw. Holding to your course still matters, but the open path isn't available now. Don't waste your strength forcing a flow that the time won't allow.
image: Heaven pulls upward, earth sinks downward, and the two move apart until nothing passes between them. When the climate turns against you, don't parade your worth or chase reward: draw in, keep your integrity quietly, and wait out the blockage without compromising yourself.
lineTexts: When one blade of grass is pulled up, others come with it, because their roots are joined. In hard times, stay connected to people of good faith, and step back together if you need to. Staying true to each other brings good fortune and, eventually, success.

Bear the situation patiently. People of small character may do well now by going along with whatever is asked of them. But if you have real worth, accept the standstill rather than compromise yourself to escape it. That's the way through, and it leads to success.

You carry a shame you can't quite name yet. Something done or intended in a time like this sits badly with you. That discomfort isn't something to push away; it's a signal worth listening to, and often the first step toward setting things right.

You act in line with what's truly right, guided by something higher than personal gain. That keeps you free of blame, even in a blocked time. People who share your values begin to gather around you, and they share in the good that follows.

The standstill is ending, and the person of real stature brings it to a close. Good fortune. But stay alert, as if saying to yourself, "What if it fails? What if it fails?" That vigilance ties success down securely, like binding it to a deep-rooted mulberry tree.

The standstill is finally overturned. First there was obstruction, and now there's joy. What was stuck gives way, and good things can begin to flow again. Your patience and integrity have carried you through, and you can step forward into what comes next.
beneficial: Your integrity, kept intact, will be ready when the way opens again.
beware: Compromising yourself to break the deadlock will cost you what matters.
reflections: Which values matter most to protect now?
Where are you tempted to compromise yourself?
What would waiting well look like?

label: Heaven over Fire
general: This is about finding your people: genuine fellowship built on shared purpose rather than private interest. The key word is openness. Real community forms in the open, where everyone can see what it stands for, not behind closed doors or in exclusive circles. That kind of fellowship can achieve great things. But harmony doesn't mean everyone being the same. It means understanding how people differ and finding the deeper ground they share. Be wary of factions, cliques, and loyalties based only on personal advantage. Ask what this group is really for. If the answer is something larger than any one person, commit to it. If not, look further.
judgment: People coming together in the open, around something shared and larger than any one of them. Fellowship that reaches this wide brings success, and even the great crossing becomes favorable. The strength here is in the openness: bonds formed in daylight, on common ground, not in private cliques.
image: Fire rises toward heaven, reaching upward toward a shared light. Build fellowship with that reach: understand how people differ, sort what truly belongs together from what doesn't, and let clear-eyed organization hold the group as one.
lineTexts: Fellowship begins at the gate, out in the open, before any private loyalties have formed. Everyone can see what it stands for. Nothing wrong comes from this. Start your connections in plain view, without secret agreements or hidden allegiances, and they'll rest on solid ground.

Fellowship limited to your own clan, your own kind, the people who already agree with you. That narrowness brings regret. A group that only includes people just like you can't reach very far, and it slowly turns into a faction rather than a community.

Weapons hidden in the thicket, climbing a high hill to keep watch, yet for three years there is no rising. Mistrust has crept into the fellowship, and suspicion keeps people apart. You can't move forward together while you're secretly bracing for a fight.

You climb the city wall but don't attack. You see that you can't win by force, and you step back from the fight before it begins. Recognizing that, and choosing reconciliation over conflict, turns things around. Good fortune.

People who belong together first weep and cry out, then laugh. Kept apart by obstacles, they struggle through grief and effort, and then at last they meet. Real union sometimes has to overcome a great deal. When it does, the joy is earned.

Fellowship in the meadow, out on the edge of town. The circle hasn't reached everyone, and the bond may feel a little distant. But there's no regret in it. Sometimes the connection that's possible is modest, and for now that's enough.
beneficial: Open, shared purpose can bring people together for something great.
beware: Cliques and private interests hollow out true fellowship.
reflections: What could bring these people together?
Which bonds here are real, and which are convenient?
How could you respect people's differences openly?

label: Fire over Heaven
general: Abundance has come to you: resources, success, recognition, influence. This is a time of great fortune, fire high in the sky shining on everything below. The question now is how you hold it. Wealth and power can make a person careless, proud, or afraid of losing what they have. The way to keep this harvest good is to stay modest and generous at the center. Use what you have to support what's right. Share it. Remember where it came from. Abundance that flows outward stays healthy; abundance that is hoarded or flaunted goes sour. You've been given a lot. Now the real work is being worthy of it.
judgment: Holding a great deal, abundance that has genuinely come to you. Supreme success. What you have now is real, and the question shifts from getting to holding well. Stay clear and generous at the center and the abundance keeps its blessing rather than curdling into excess.
image: Fire blazes high above heaven, its light reaching everything below. With so much within your power, use the clarity it gives you: check what's harmful, encourage what's good, and align yourself with the better order of things instead of letting plenty make you careless.
lineTexts: Abundance has only just begun, and nothing harmful has touched you yet. There's no blame here. Keep in mind how hard it is to handle plenty well; pride and carelessness creep in quietly. Stay aware of the difficulty, and you'll remain without blame.

A big wagon, well built and fully loaded. You have the capacity to carry a great deal: resources, responsibility, people who depend on you. You can move forward with it in any direction, because you're strong enough for the load. No blame.

A prince brings his wealth as an offering to the Son of Heaven. Great abundance is meant to serve something higher than yourself. A person of small character couldn't do this; they would cling to it, and it would sour. Let what you have serve a larger good.

You hold back from displaying your wealth and power, and you don't compete with those around you to show what you have. Living alongside abundance without making it the center of who you are keeps you clear of envy and mistakes. No blame.

Your sincerity is met by sincerity from everyone around you. People trust you because you're genuine. Be open and approachable, but carry yourself with real dignity too, so that warmth doesn't slide into carelessness. That balance brings good fortune.

Heaven itself blesses you. Abundance held with modesty and good faith aligns you with something larger than your own effort. Good fortune, and nothing that doesn't turn out well. This is what plenty looks like when it's held rightly.
beneficial: Real abundance has come; use it generously to support what's right.
beware: Plenty breeds carelessness and pride; hoarded wealth goes sour.
reflections: What has come to you that you didn't have before?
Who else could your good fortune help?
Where might plenty make you careless?

label: Earth over Mountain
general: Modesty, the real kind. Not false humility or putting yourself down, but strength that doesn't need to be seen. Picture a mountain hidden inside the earth: vast, but content to stay low. Tradition notes that every one of this hexagram's six lines is favorable, which is rare, and says a lot about what modesty brings. When you don't need to announce your worth, people trust you, and things flow toward you naturally. Modesty also has a balancing quality: it takes from where there's too much and gives where there's too little. Ask yourself where you might be inflating yourself, or where you're holding back from giving. Carry what you have lightly, and you can carry it far.
judgment: True modesty, the mountain content to sit below the earth though it towers within it. There's real success in this, and it lasts. The person who has much and still doesn't need to display it carries things through to a good end. Not smallness, but strength that feels no need to announce itself.
image: The mountain holds itself low, hidden inside the earth though it is vast. Take after it: draw down from where there's too much and add where there's too little, evening things out quietly, measuring fairly without making a show of it.
lineTexts: Modest about your modesty, so quiet about it that even humility isn't worn as a badge. You simply do what needs doing without fuss. With this, even crossing the great water, taking on something difficult and important, becomes possible. Good fortune.

Modesty that has come to expression. People notice it in how you speak and act without your ever announcing it. It's become part of who you are. Staying steady and true with that, good fortune follows naturally.

Modest even in your accomplishments. You've done real work and earned real merit, and you don't make a show of it. People respect that, and they'll support you to the end. Carrying achievement lightly brings things to a good conclusion. Good fortune.

Modesty in action, everywhere you move. Nothing is unfavorable here. Don't let humility become a hiding place, an excuse to hold back; let it shape what you actually do. Keep stirring it into your conduct, not just your view of yourself.

You don't boast of your wealth to your neighbors, and though you're not rich, people follow your lead. Modesty isn't weakness, though. Sometimes force is needed to set things right, and when it is, use it without hesitation. Everything turns out favorably.

Modesty so well known it's recognized everywhere. Now you have the standing to act with real force. Turn that strength first to setting your own house in order, the old image of disciplining one's own city rather than attacking others.
beneficial: Quiet strength without display earns trust and carries things to a good end.
beware: Watch for hidden pride, or for false humility that holds back giving.
reflections: What could you do well without needing credit?
Where is there too much, or too little?
How would it feel to carry this success lightly?

label: Thunder over Earth
general: Energy is rising, and it's contagious. Thunder bursts from the earth; people want to move, celebrate, get going. This is the kind of enthusiasm that can carry a group forward, inspire action, and make hard things feel possible. Use it. Now is a good time to bring helpers on board, start things, rally support. But enthusiasm needs direction. It works best when it follows the natural flow of things, the way music moves people because it has rhythm and form. Without that, it turns into empty excitement or self-indulgence. Ask what this energy is for. Channel it into something real and it can take you far. Waste it, and it scatters as fast as it came.
judgment: A gathered, contagious energy, the kind that moves people to act together. This is the moment to appoint helpers and set things in motion, to channel the shared mood into real organized effort. Enthusiasm aligned with the natural flow carries easily; waste it and the moment disperses.
image: Thunder breaks from the earth and the air comes alive with movement. Meet that rising energy the way music gathers a crowd: give it form and rhythm, honor what deserves honoring, and let a shared devotion lift people into motion together.
lineTexts: You announce your enthusiasm loudly, boasting of your good luck or your powerful connections. That brings misfortune. Excitement that needs an audience is usually hollow, and bragging about favor from above invites resentment from everyone around you.

Firm as a rock. You don't get swept up in the excitement around you; you see what's coming before it arrives, and you act on it without waiting a whole day. That clear, steady perception, the opposite of mood-driven zeal, brings good fortune.

You look upward, waiting for others to give you enthusiasm and approval. Dependent excitement like this brings regret, and hesitating too long makes it worse. If you're waiting for someone else to light the spark, look for the source within yourself.

You are the source of the enthusiasm, the one others gather around. Great things can be achieved through you. Don't let doubt or suspicion in. If you trust and stay sincere, friends come together around you like strands of hair held in a clasp.

Persistently ill, yet you don't die. Something keeps pressing on you, a constant strain that prevents you from being swept up in the general excitement. It's uncomfortable, but that pressure may be exactly what keeps you clear-headed, and safe.

Lost in enthusiasm, carried away by the mood of the moment, your judgment clouded. But even now, even after things have taken their course, if you change direction there's no blame. It's never too late to wake up and see clearly.
beneficial: Shared enthusiasm can rally people and make hard things feel possible.
beware: Energy without direction scatters as quickly as it came.
reflections: What is this energy really for?
Who could you bring along now?
What would keep the momentum going?

label: Lake over Thunder
general: This is a time to follow rather than lead, to adapt yourself to what the moment needs. That's harder than it sounds. Following well means letting go of your own agenda for a while, reading the situation, and moving with it. It doesn't mean giving up your values or trailing after whoever is loudest. The key is what you follow: follow what's genuinely right, and you'll find success. There's also a lesson about rhythm here. Thunder rests in the lake as the year darkens; rest when it's time to rest. People who know how to follow often make the best leaders later, because they understand what it takes. For now, be flexible, be open, and let the right direction lead you.
judgment: To lead well, you first learn to follow, and this is a time for following. Not blind obedience, but adapting yourself to what the moment genuinely asks, the way a good guest reads a room. That brings real success, as long as what you follow is worth following. Stay true to what's right while you yield, and nothing here will be held against you.
image: Thunder has gone quiet in the middle of the lake, its energy resting under the water as the year turns toward winter. Follow the rhythm of the season the same way: when evening comes, go inside, rest and recover, instead of pushing against a time that is asking you to stop.
lineTexts: What you follow is changing, and that's not a betrayal as long as you stay true to what's right. Step outside your usual circle, beyond your own gate, and meet people openly rather than only among those who already agree with you. Following that reaches outward like this brings real achievement and good fortune.

The traditional image is clinging to the little boy and letting go of the grown man. Attach yourself to what is small and easy, and you lose what is mature and worth following. You can't hold both at once. Be careful where you give your loyalty, because the lesser bond quietly crowds out the greater one.

Now the choice runs the other way: you hold to the grown man and let the little boy go. Following what is mature gets you what you seek, though it costs you something you'll miss. Stay steady and honest in the choice, so it serves what's right and not just what's convenient.

People are following you, and that success carries its own danger. A following built on flattery or self-interest turns sour, even if your intentions are good. Stay sincere and make your purpose plain to everyone. Clarity about what you truly stand for keeps you from going wrong.

Your trust goes to what is genuinely good, and you follow it wholeheartedly. This is following at its best: sincere, clear-eyed, devoted to excellence rather than to convenience or power. When you give yourself to something worthy, good fortune follows.

The bond is now held fast, tied and bound, as firm as a vow. The traditional image is the king making offerings on the western mountain: a loyalty so deep it becomes sacred. Even if part of you wants to step back, you're drawn in further. Honor what you're bound to, and let it carry you.
beneficial: Adapting to what the moment asks brings success and trust.
beware: Follow only what is worth following; don't lose your values along the way.
reflections: What is this moment asking you to follow?
How can you adapt without losing yourself?
Where would rest help more than effort?

label: Mountain over Wind

names.wilhelm: Work on What Has Been Spoiled

general: Something has gone wrong through neglect: a situation, a relationship, a habit, perhaps something you inherited from the past. It has spoiled slowly, like food left too long. The good news is that this hexagram is about repair, and repair is possible. Don't despair, and don't just complain about how it got this way. Get to work. Take time first to understand the causes, then act decisively, then take time afterward to make sure the new arrangement holds. This often means confronting old patterns, including patterns passed down to you. It takes energy and honesty, but the effort pays off. What was decaying can become the ground for something healthy.
judgment: Something has gone bad through neglect, like food left too long in a bowl. The good news is that this can be repaired, and the repair itself brings success. It may even call for a bold undertaking. But work carefully at both ends: take time to understand how it went wrong before you start, and take time to watch over the new arrangement afterward, so the decay doesn't creep back.
image: The wind sweeps low around the foot of the mountain, stirring the stale air and setting things moving. Repair begins the same way: shake loose what has stagnated in people, then steady them, renewing their spirit so the change can hold.
lineTexts: The traditional image is a son setting right what his father let spoil. You're dealing with damage you inherited: from family, from a predecessor, from an old way of doing things. Taking it on carries risk, but if you're capable and honest, the repair redeems the past instead of shaming it. Good fortune in the end.

The traditional image is setting right what the mother let spoil, and it calls for a gentler hand. Some inherited damage is tender, bound up with care and loyalty. Being rigid or harsh in correcting it would do more harm than the original fault. Repair with tact and patience rather than force.

You set right what the father spoiled, and this time you push a little too hard. There may be friction, small regrets, the sense of having overcorrected. But doing too much here is better than doing nothing. No great harm comes of it, and the work moves forward.

You look on what your father spoiled with indulgence, letting it slide because confronting it feels too uncomfortable. Keep going this way and the damage spreads, and you'll come to regret it. Tolerating decay isn't kindness. It only hands the problem to someone else, larger.

You set right what the father spoiled, and this time you have the means and the support to do it well. People recognize the repair and praise it, because you chose the right help and the right methods. This is how old wrongs are truly mended.

You don't serve kings or lords; you set yourself higher aims of your own. Not every repair is yours to make. Sometimes the right work is to cultivate your own values and keep your distance from affairs that aren't yours to fix. This is a dignified withdrawal, not neglect.
beneficial: What was spoiled can be repaired, and the repair brings renewal.
beware: Fix the causes, not just the symptoms, or the decay returns.
reflections: What has been neglected here?
Which old habits keep the problem going?
What would make the repair last?

label: Earth over Lake
general: Something good is drawing near. Growth is coming, influence is increasing, and things are moving in your favor, like the year turning toward spring. This is a time of real promise, and it's worth acting on. Approach people and opportunities with warmth and sincerity; your presence can genuinely help others now. But the hexagram carries a reminder: this rise has a season. What grows will also wane. Don't let the good time make you careless or assume it will last forever. Use the momentum to build something solid, and prepare now for the turning that will eventually come. Then it won't catch you off guard.
judgment: Something good is drawing near, a season of growth and rising strength, and you're moving into a position of influence. It brings great success if you stay steady and true. But every spring has its turning, and this upswing won't last forever. Act on it now, and prepare for the time when it reverses.
image: The earth rises above the lake, bordering it closely and watching over it. Approach people that way: be tireless in teaching and generous in protecting, with a patience that doesn't run out.
lineTexts: You approach together with others, side by side, and the shared momentum carries you forward. Good influence spreads when it's joined by people who think alike. Stay steady and true to your purpose as you go, and this joint approach brings good fortune.

Again you advance in good company, and now everything favors you. You don't need to worry yet about the turning that will eventually come; the moment fully supports you. Act on it with confidence. Good fortune, and whatever you undertake goes well.

You approach too easily, pleased with yourself, making things comfortable instead of real. That kind of smooth, careless influence leads nowhere good. But once you notice it and start to genuinely care about doing better, the mistake can be undone. Concern turns this around, and there's no blame.

You approach in the most complete way: sincerely, wholeheartedly, meeting people on their own ground without holding yourself above them. Openness like this makes connection easy and builds real trust. No blame.

You approach with wisdom, the way a great leader does: knowing what you can't do yourself and trusting capable people to do it. Choosing the right helpers and then letting them work is the mark of real authority. Good fortune.

You approach with generosity and honest warmth, perhaps returning to help others when you no longer need to for yourself. That big-heartedness, given freely from a place of experience, brings good fortune and no blame.
beneficial: Growth and influence are rising; a time of real promise.
beware: Every rise has its season; prepare now for when it turns.
reflections: What good thing is coming closer?
What could you build in this good season?
How can you prepare for when it changes?

label: Wind over Earth
general: Step back and look. This hexagram is like a tower overlooking the land: a place from which you can see clearly, and also be seen. Before you act, observe your situation, the people involved, your own motives. Real understanding comes from attention, not hurry. At the same time, you may be someone others are watching, and what they see matters more than what you say. Like someone at a ceremony, composed and sincere, you influence people by who you are rather than by persuasion. Ask yourself what you are really looking at, and what you're showing. Contemplation now leads to wiser action later.
judgment: A moment of looking, and of being looked at. Like someone at a ceremony who has washed their hands but not yet made the offering, the real power lies in the stillness just before acting, when attention is fully gathered. Hold that sincere, collected presence and others will trust you without needing to be told why.
image: The wind moves across the whole earth, touching everything it passes. Take time to really look at your situation and the people in it, moving among them and seeing them clearly, before you decide what guidance to give.
lineTexts: The traditional image is the way a child looks at things, seeing only the surface. For someone with no responsibility, that's no fault. But if you're meant to lead or decide, a naive, shallow view will cost you. Look deeper than first impressions before you act.

The traditional image is peering out through a crack in the door. A view that narrow was once considered enough for someone kept inside the house. If you're meant to act in the wider world, a keyhole perspective isn't enough. Open the door and look at the whole picture.

You turn your eyes on your own life: what you've done, where it has led, which way to go next. This honest self-observation tells you whether to advance or to step back. Let what you actually see decide, not what you wish were true.

You look at the wider world at its best, at how things are run when they're run well, and you see where you could contribute. This is the moment to offer your abilities to someone who can use them, to be the king's welcome guest. Your gifts have a place.
You contemplate your own life by looking at its effects on others. The people around you show what kind of influence you really have. If what you see is good, you're on the right path. No blame.

You contemplate your life once more, now free of personal ambition, simply asking whether your character is what it should be. This is watching at its most searching, an inner examination with nothing left to prove. It keeps you from error. No blame.
beneficial: Stepping back to observe clearly will lead to wiser action.
beware: Others are watching; your conduct speaks louder than your words.
reflections: What do you notice when you just watch?
What are your actions showing others?
What are your real motives here?

label: Fire over Thunder
general: Something is in the way, an obstacle that keeps things from coming together, like something caught between the teeth. It won't go away by itself, and ignoring it won't help. It needs to be bitten through: dealt with directly, firmly, decisively. That can mean confronting a problem, ending a pattern, naming a lie, or setting a clear consequence. The image is thunder and lightning, force combined with clarity. Be energetic, but be fair. Know exactly what the problem is before you act, and respond in proportion. Once the obstacle is gone, the parts that were held apart can come together again. Don't avoid the bite; it's what makes union possible.
judgment: Something is blocking the way, like an obstacle caught between the teeth that keeps the jaws from closing. It won't dissolve on its own; it needs to be bitten through, firmly and decisively. This brings success. It's a time for clear judgment and fair consequences, dealing with what's wrong so that things can come together again.
image: Thunder and lightning arrive together, force and clarity at once. Bring both to the problem: make your boundaries clear and your consequences fair, so that what's right is plain and what's wrong can be dealt with.
lineTexts: The traditional image is feet locked in the stocks, the toes hidden. A small wrong is caught and corrected early, with a light consequence. That's a mercy: the first mistake checked before it can grow into a habit. No blame.

Biting through soft meat, so deep the nose disappears into it. The task is easier than you expected and you go at it with too much force, overdoing the correction. Still, what you're dealing with justifies a firm response. No blame.

Gnawing old dried meat, you hit something rotten. You're tackling a problem without quite the authority to settle it, and it bites back with some resistance or embarrassment. Small regret. But the cause is right, so there's no real blame.

Gnawing dried meat on the bone, you find metal arrowheads: a hard, stubborn task with real resistance. Stay aware of how difficult it is, and stay firm and straight as an arrow. Persevere like this and good fortune follows.

Gnawing dried lean meat, you find yellow gold. The problem is serious but not hopeless, and you're in a position to deal with it fairly. Be true and impartial, like gold, and stay aware of the danger. No blame.

The traditional image is a neck locked in a wooden collar, the ears hidden. You've stopped listening; warnings go unheard, and one wrong builds on another until correction can no longer reach you. Misfortune. Open your ears while you still can.
beneficial: Dealing firmly with the obstacle lets things come together again.
beware: Ignoring the problem won't make it go away; respond fairly, not harshly.
reflections: What is standing in the way?
How could you deal with it firmly but fairly?
What have you been avoiding?

label: Mountain over Fire
general: Beauty matters. Form, style, grace: they make life pleasant, help us connect, and give shape to what we feel. This hexagram celebrates that, but it also asks you to see it clearly. Grace is like firelight on a mountain: lovely and illuminating, but it doesn't change the mountain itself. Adornment works well for small things. It can't substitute for substance when the big questions come up. If you're dealing with appearances right now, how you present yourself, how a project looks, how others seem, enjoy the beauty but look past it too. Ask what lies underneath. True grace is when the outside honestly reflects the inside.
judgment: Beauty and form, the grace that makes things pleasing. It brings success, but on a modest scale: style serves small undertakings well, not as the foundation of large ones. Enjoy what's beautiful here and let it lift you, without mistaking a lovely surface for the substance underneath.
image: A fire burns at the foot of the mountain, lighting up its slopes, though it can't reach far into the dark. Let grace help you handle everyday matters with care and clarity, but don't rely on it to settle the serious questions; those need more than a beautiful light.
lineTexts: You adorn your feet and choose to walk rather than ride in a carriage that isn't yours. You'd rather move by your own effort than accept a comfort that would compromise you. Simple, dignified beginnings are worth more than flashy shortcuts.

The traditional image is grooming the beard: an ornament that only exists because of the face beneath it. Form is lovely, but it follows substance and depends on it. Attend to what's underneath first, and let the grace serve it rather than stand in for it.

You're graceful and glowing, softened by a moment of comfort and favor. Enjoy it, but don't sink into it. Pleasant ease can quietly dissolve your resolve. Stay steady and true beneath the shine, and the good fortune lasts.

Adorned only in white, as if on a white horse with wings: a choice between showy grace and plain sincerity. The one approaching isn't a robber but someone seeking a genuine bond. Choose the simple, true connection over the dazzling one.

In the gardens on the hill, you bring only a small roll of silk. Your offering seems meager, even embarrassing next to the splendor around you. But sincerity counts for more than display. What feels like humiliation now ends in good fortune.

Simple white as your only ornament. Grace at its highest has no need for decoration at all; the plain thing, honestly itself, is enough. Let go of trying to impress, and let substance speak. No blame.
beneficial: Beauty and grace lift everyday life and help you connect.
beware: Don't mistake a lovely surface for substance on serious matters.
reflections: What is beautiful here?
What lies under the surface?
Where might looks be hiding what matters?

label: Mountain over Earth
general: Things are breaking down. Like a house whose foundations are wearing away, a structure in your life is collapsing, slowly but steadily. It's not the time to fight it, make bold moves, or try to hold everything together through sheer effort. The forces at work are larger than you right now. Instead, accept what is passing. Lie low. Protect what's essential and let go of what isn't. The image offers a clue: the mountain stands on the earth, and it stays standing only if its base is broad. Strengthen your foundation: your health, your closest relationships, your core values. Decline is part of the cycle, and it makes room for what comes next.
judgment: Things are falling away, the way a structure gives as its supports wear down from beneath. The decline isn't your doing, and right now action can't stop it. This is not the time to set out or push forward. Lie low, let it run its course, and save your strength for what comes after.
image: The mountain rests on the earth, and it stands only as long as its base is broad and solid. When things are crumbling, strengthen the foundation: be generous to those who depend on you, and build security from the ground up.
lineTexts: The bed is split at the legs: decay has started at the very foundation, where people least notice it. Whatever is undermining the good is gaining ground, and integrity is being worn away. Misfortune. Little can be done yet except to see it clearly and hold on to what you value.

Now the bed is split at the frame, closer to where you rest. The danger is nearer, and you have few allies. Misfortune. Be careful and flexible; don't plant yourself stubbornly in the way of something you can't stop.

You find yourself among those tearing things down, but you're not truly one of them. Breaking with the people around you to stay loyal to what's right may cost you their company. Even so, it's the right choice. No blame.

The bed is split all the way to the skin. The decline has reached you personally, and there's no stepping aside from it now. Misfortune. What remains is to endure, protect your core, and wait for the turning that follows every fall.

The traditional image is a string of fish, led in order like attendants receiving the palace's favor. The forces that were wearing things down now line up willingly behind what's right, and order begins to return. Everything goes well from here.

One great fruit is left on the tree, uneaten: the seed of renewal survives. People with integrity find themselves carried again by those around them, as if in a carriage. Those who live by tearing down only wreck their own homes. After the falling away, the seed sprouts.
beneficial: Letting go of what's failing makes room for what comes next.
beware: Fighting the decline or making bold moves now will only cost you.
reflections: What is falling away?
What foundation needs your care right now?
What might this ending make room for?

label: Earth over Thunder
general: After a long darkness, the light returns. This is the winter solstice among the hexagrams: the moment when the days stop shortening and begin, slowly, to lengthen. Something that had been lost or dormant is coming back: energy, hope, a relationship, a sense of direction. It isn't dramatic. It's quiet and natural, and the first stirrings are fragile. Don't rush it or test it too soon. Give it rest and protection so it can gather strength. This is also a hexagram of returning to yourself, coming back to the right path after straying. The way back is open. Take it gently, and let the return grow in its own time.
judgment: The turning point. After a time of decline the light begins to return, as surely as the days lengthen after the winter solstice. It brings success. The movement is natural and unforced, so there's no need to hurry it. Old friends come back, energy returns in its own rhythm, and it's good now to have somewhere to go.
image: Thunder stirs deep inside the earth, the first faint movement of returning life, still hidden. Protect that new beginning the way the ancients rested at midwinter: keep things quiet, don't scatter your energy, and let the return gather strength before you test it.
lineTexts: You turn back after only a small step off the path, before any real harm is done. Catching yourself early is the best kind of return. There's nothing to be sorry for. Great good fortune.

A quiet, graceful return, helped along by good company and good examples. It's easier to come back to yourself when someone worth following shows the way. Let yourself be guided by what is kind and right. Good fortune.

You keep returning, again and again: straying, coming back, straying again. It's a precarious pattern, unsteady and tiring, and it carries danger. But each return still counts, and you haven't given up. No blame, though steadier footing would serve you far better.

Walking in the middle of others, you turn back alone. The crowd goes one way and you quietly choose your own path back to what's right. It may be lonely, but it's true, and it needs no one's approval.

A noble return. You look honestly at yourself, take full responsibility for where you went wrong, and come back without excuses or self-pity. Turning back with that kind of integrity, openly and generously, leaves nothing to regret.

You miss the return entirely, holding stubbornly to the wrong path. Misfortune and trouble come from every side. Leading others this way would end in a defeat that takes years to repair. The moment to turn back has slipped past; recognize it before it costs more.
beneficial: The light is returning; energy and direction come back naturally.
beware: The new beginning is fragile; don't rush it or test it too soon.
reflections: What is starting to come back?
How can you protect this fresh start?
Which path is calling you back?

label: Heaven over Thunder
general: Act from the heart, without calculation. This hexagram is about innocence in its truest sense: doing what is right because it's right, not because of what you'll get from it. When you act this way, in tune with the natural order of things, success follows. Trouble comes when you start scheming, manipulating, or bending the truth to get an outcome. The hexagram also carries a warning about the unexpected: even when you're acting rightly, things can go sideways for reasons you didn't cause. Don't let that push you into anxiety or control. Stay sincere, accept what comes, and don't force your plans on a situation that's asking for honesty and openness instead.
judgment: Acting without hidden motives, simply and naturally, the way things move when nothing false gets in the way. That brings great success, as long as you stay true. But the moment you start scheming or bending the truth, even a little, things go wrong, and pushing ahead then only makes it worse. Keep your intentions clean and let the situation unfold.
image: Thunder rolls beneath the open sky, and everything it reaches stirs awake in its own natural way. Live in tune with that: respond to the season you're actually in, and help what's around you grow according to its own nature rather than your plans for it.
lineTexts: You act from innocence, without calculation or hidden motive, simply doing what feels true. Your first impulse here is a good one; trust it. Moving forward in that open, uncomplicated spirit is exactly right. Good fortune.

The traditional image is reaping without having plowed, harvesting a field you didn't clear with the harvest in mind. Do each thing for its own sake, without fixing your eyes on the reward, and things go well wherever you turn.

Undeserved misfortune. Someone's tethered ox is taken by a passerby, and the villagers nearby are blamed for it. Even innocence can't always protect you from bad luck or unfair suspicion. It isn't your fault. Accept it without bitterness and don't let it make you cynical.
Stay true and steady to what you know is right. What genuinely belongs to you can't be taken away, and you don't need to grasp at anything else. Hold your ground quietly. No blame.
An illness has come though you've done nothing wrong. Don't reach for drastic remedies or force a cure; it will pass of itself. Let nature take its course, without panic, and joy returns.
Even innocent action brings trouble now. The timing isn't right, and pushing forward despite your good intentions only leads to harm. This is a moment to wait. Nothing you force will help.
beneficial: Acting sincerely, without hidden motives, aligns you with how things want to go.
beware: Scheming backfires, and the unexpected can still happen; don't cling to control.
reflections: What would you do without any hidden agenda?
Where might you be bending the truth?
How can you handle surprises without grabbing control?

label: Mountain over Heaven

names.wilhelm: The Taming Power of the Great

general: There's great power here, held back and stored up, like the strength of heaven contained within a mountain. You've built up energy, knowledge, resources, or skill. Now you're asked to hold it with discipline rather than spend it all at once. That kind of restraint isn't weakness; it's what turns raw strength into something useful. Keep learning. Draw on the wisdom of those who came before you; their experience can shape your character. And when you're ready, don't keep it all at home. This is a good time to put your accumulated strength to work in the world, even on something ambitious. The mountain holds heaven's power so it can be released at the right time.
judgment: Great strength held in and gathered up, like a powerful horse kept steady under a firm hand. The stored energy is a gift, and staying disciplined with it brings success. This isn't a time to keep it all at home; put it to use in the wider world. Even a great undertaking is favorable now.
image: Heaven sits inside the mountain, a vast power held within something still. Build your inner strength the same way: learn from what people have said and done before you, and let that store of wisdom shape your character.
lineTexts: Danger is close. Stop, and hold your strength in reserve; pressing forward now invites harm. Restraint at the very beginning is the advantage here, even if it frustrates you. Wait until the way is clear.

The traditional image is a wagon with the axle-straps removed. You're held back by something stronger than you, and for now that's for the best. Instead of struggling against it, let the pause build your strength. You'll move when the wheels are back on.

Good horses running free: the restraint is lifting and the way is opening. Stay aware of the danger, and keep training daily, in care, skill and self-defense. With that discipline, it's good to have somewhere to go, and you can advance.

The traditional image is a board fixed over a young bull's horns before they grow. Restrain wild strength early, while it's still easy and no one has been hurt. Prevention at this stage costs little and saves much. Great good fortune.

The traditional image is the tusk of a gelded boar: the dangerous force tamed at its root, not just held back on the surface. You've dealt with the cause instead of fighting the symptoms. Good fortune.
