You reach the open way of heaven. The holding back is over; the strength you've patiently stored up now flows freely, and things open up in every direction. What you gathered through restraint is ready to be used. Success.
beneficial: Stored strength and learning are ready to be put to good use.
beware: Power spent without discipline goes to waste.
reflections: What strength have you been building up?
Whose experience could guide you?
When will it be time to use what you've stored?

label: Mountain over Thunder
general: Look at what you feed, and what feeds you. This hexagram takes the shape of an open mouth, and it asks about nourishment in every sense: food, ideas, relationships, habits, what you take in, the support you give others. What you hunger for reveals who you are. Are you feeding the parts of yourself, and of the people around you, that are worth growing? Or what's easiest, loudest, or most immediately satisfying? Be mindful of what goes in and what comes out: what you eat and drink, and what you say. Care for yourself and others with attention, and choose your nourishment deliberately. Good nourishment, steadily given, brings good fortune.
judgment: Nourishment, both what you take in and what you give. Look closely at what you feed: your body, your mind, the people who depend on you. Look too at what you hunger for, because what someone seeks to fill themselves with reveals who they are. Tend to this carefully and steadily, and good fortune follows.
image: Thunder stirs at the foot of the mountain, the way the jaw moves below the still face. Take care with what goes out of your mouth and what goes in: be thoughtful in your words, and moderate in what you eat and drink.
lineTexts: The traditional image is letting go of your own magic tortoise and gazing hungrily at someone else, jaw hanging. You give up the resources you already have and envy what others own. That brings misfortune. Trust what genuinely nourishes you, and stop measuring it against other people's plates.

You look for nourishment in the wrong place: leaning on others when you could support yourself, or reaching toward the heights for what should come from your own ground. Continuing like this leads to misfortune. Learn to sustain yourself.

You turn away from what truly nourishes you and grasp at what satisfies only for a moment. However determined you are, this brings misfortune, and for ten years nothing good will come of it. Change course before the habit hardens.

Now you look upward for nourishment for the right reasons: seeking help so you can care for others. Search for the right helpers with the fixed, unblinking gaze of a tiger, and keep after it. Good fortune, and no blame.

You turn from the usual path. You don't have the strength yet to nourish others alone, so you rely on someone wiser and steadier. Staying steady in that brings good fortune. But this isn't the time to cross great waters or take on huge undertakings.

You are the source others draw nourishment from. That's a heavy and precarious responsibility, and you know it. Stay aware of the danger, and good fortune follows. Now it's favorable to cross the great water.
beneficial: Mindful nourishment, for yourself and others, brings good fortune.
beware: What you hunger for reveals you; feed what's worth growing.
reflections: What are you feeding in yourself and others?
What are you hungry for here?
Which words need more care?

label: Lake over Wind
general: Something is carrying more weight than it can bear. The ridgepole is bending; the situation is overloaded. It could be a workload, a relationship, a responsibility, or a belief that can't hold up much longer. The hexagram's shape shows it: strong in the middle, weak at both ends. The danger is real, but this isn't a time to freeze. Exceptional circumstances call for exceptional action. Look for ways to shift the burden, find support, or make a decisive change before something breaks. You may need to stand alone, act against convention, or step away from the crowd. Do it calmly. Courage now means being willing to move when others would rather wait.
judgment: Too much weight on too little support, like a roof beam bending under a load it was never meant to carry. Something has to give. This is an exceptional moment and it calls for exceptional action: don't freeze, move. Handle the strain wisely, finding a way to shift the load before it breaks, and you come through.
image: The lake has risen so high that the trees stand drowned beneath it. In times this extraordinary, stand firm even if you stand alone. Hold to what you know is right without fear, and if you have to step back from the world for a while, do it without regret.
lineTexts: Spreading soft white rushes beneath things before you set them down. Extraordinary times call for extraordinary care. Be cautious, prepare thoroughly, and handle what's fragile gently at the start. No blame.

The traditional image is a dry willow putting out new shoots: an old man taking a young wife. Something worn renews itself by joining with what is fresh and humble. This unexpected union brings real vitality. Everything goes well.

The ridgepole sags to the breaking point. You force ahead without listening to anyone, and the strain cracks the structure you're trying to hold up. Misfortune. Pushing harder now only makes the collapse more certain.

The ridgepole is braced and holds. You carry the weight well, supported from below, and the structure stays sound. Good fortune. But if you start using the moment for other ends or personal gain, it turns into humiliation.

The traditional image is a dry willow bursting into flower: an old woman taking a young husband. It's a showy blossoming that bears no fruit, vitality spent on the surface without renewing the roots. Ask whether what's flowering in your life can actually grow. No blame, but no praise either.

Wading into deep water until it closes over your head. You dare beyond your strength for something worth it, and it costs you. Misfortune, yet no blame: some causes are worth the price, and there's honor in having tried.
beneficial: Decisive action now can relieve a burden before it breaks.
beware: The load is too heavy; freezing or ignoring the strain is the real danger.
reflections: What is carrying too much weight?
What change could ease the load?
Where might you need to stand alone?

label: Water over Water
general: Danger, and then more danger, like water rushing from one pit into the next. This is one of the hardest hexagrams, but it carries a clear teaching: the way through is to be like water. Water doesn't stop at a difficult place, and it doesn't lose itself either. It fills the hollow, then flows on, always remaining water. In the same way, stay true to yourself in the middle of difficulty. Don't get used to the danger or start believing it's normal, and don't panic. Sincerity holds you steady. Take the next step, then the next. Keep doing what's right, keep learning, keep moving. You will come through, and you'll come through knowing your own depth.
judgment: Danger repeated, one pit after another, like water rushing through a ravine. There's no way around it, only through. What carries you is sincerity, an inner steadiness the danger can't touch. Keep faith with yourself, keep moving the way water keeps moving, and whatever you do will succeed.
image: Water flows on and on, filling every hollow before it moves ahead, never stopping until it reaches the sea. Let your character be that consistent: keep living by what you value, and keep learning and teaching, steadily and without breaks.
lineTexts: Deeper into the pit: repeated danger has become familiar, and you start to settle into it. Getting used to the danger is the real danger, because you stop looking for the way out. Misfortune. Don't let difficulty become your home.

In the middle of the abyss, danger all around. Don't try to escape everything at once. Aim for small gains, one step at a time, and take each bit of ground you can win. Little by little is how you climb out.
Danger ahead and danger behind, and every move leads deeper into the pit. Stop. Struggling now only digs you in further. Stay still until you can see a real way out.

A jug of wine, a bowl of rice, plain earthen vessels passed simply through the window. In danger, sincerity matters more than ceremony. Offer and accept help directly and honestly, without formality. In the end, no blame.
The pit isn't overflowing; the water only rises to the rim. Don't try to do more than get through this safely. Calm, steady flow is enough for now. No blame.

Bound with ropes and shut in among thorns, you've lost your way so completely that for three years you can't find it again. Misfortune. This is where losing touch with what's right leads. Ask honestly where you stopped seeing clearly.
beneficial: Like water, you can flow through this; sincerity will hold you steady.
beware: Don't get used to the danger, and don't panic; keep moving, step by step.
reflections: What is your next step through this?
What keeps you steady when it gets hard?
Which danger have you started to get used to?

label: Fire over Fire
general: Clarity, warmth, the light of understanding. Fire needs something to hold on to, wood to burn, a source to cling to, and so does your own light. This hexagram asks what you're attached to, and whether it sustains you. Bright things can burn out quickly if they're not grounded. Find what nourishes your clarity: truth, good relationships, meaningful work. The old text says that caring for a cow brings good fortune, a picture of gentle, patient strength. Brilliance works best when it's combined with that kind of steadiness. Let your light be warm rather than harsh, and let it help others see more clearly rather than just showing what you can do.
judgment: Brightness, the light that needs something to cling to, the way a flame needs wood. Clarity and warmth come from being rightly attached: to what is true, to what sustains you. Stay steady and gentle, willing and docile like a well-tended cow, and this brings success and good fortune.
image: The sun rises, sets, and rises again, light renewing itself day after day. Let your own clarity work the same way: keep it burning steadily, so its light reaches outward and helps others see.
lineTexts: Footsteps crisscross at the start of the day; impressions rush in from all sides and it's easy to scatter. Stay collected and respectful, take things in carefully, and you'll find your direction. No blame.

Yellow light, the color of the middle way. Your clarity is balanced and moderate, neither glaring nor dim, and it rests on what's true rather than on show. Light like this warms without burning. Supreme good fortune.

In the light of the setting sun, you either beat the pot and sing, or lament that old age is coming. Everything passes; that's not a tragedy. Clinging to it, or despairing over it, both bring misfortune. Enjoy the light that's left.
A sudden blaze that flares up, burns out, and is thrown away. Brilliance with no staying power consumes itself fast and leaves nothing behind. Misfortune. Don't let your light become a flash.
Tears in floods, sighing and grieving. You feel deeply how fragile and fleeting everything is, even at the height of things. That honest sorrow transforms you instead of breaking you. Good fortune.
The king sends you out to set things right. You deal with the ringleaders and spare those who merely followed. Clarity used to end what's wrong, without cruelty or excess. No blame.
beneficial: Clarity and warmth grow when you hold on to what truly sustains you.
beware: Brightness without grounding burns out quickly.
reflections: What keeps your mind clear here?
What are you holding on to?
How could your understanding help others see?

label: Lake over Mountain
general: Two forces are drawn to each other. This hexagram opens the second half of the I Ching, which turns from the order of heaven and earth to human relationships, and it begins with attraction. It can be romance, friendship, or any connection where people genuinely influence each other. The key is mutuality. Influence works best when it's open and receptive, not forced or manipulative. Think of a lake on a mountain: the mountain makes space, and the water fills it. If you want to connect with someone, make room for them. Listen as much as you speak. Attraction based on sincerity can grow into something lasting. Be careful only of influence that's shallow, rushed, or one-sided.
judgment: Attraction, the quiet pull between two people or two forces that moves them toward each other. It brings success when it rests on something true. The strength here is openness: real influence happens when you're receptive rather than pushing, the way a good relationship begins with mutual willingness.
image: A lake rests on top of a mountain, the high ground holding still water in its hollow. Make room in yourself the same way: stay open and humble enough to receive others, and they'll be drawn to you.
lineTexts: Influence in the big toe: a first stirring that hasn't moved anything yet. The desire is there, but nothing is visible to anyone, maybe not even to you. Neither good nor bad, just a beginning. Notice it before you act on it.
Influence in the calves: you want to move before it's time, carried along by impulse. Running ahead of yourself brings misfortune. Staying where you are until the moment is right brings good fortune.

Influence in the thighs: you cling to whatever moves you and follow other people's impulses without your own judgment. Going on this way leads to humiliation. Find your own footing before you follow anyone.

Steadiness brings good fortune, and regret disappears. But if your mind is restless, constantly scheming how to sway people, only those you deliberately reach will follow. Real influence is quiet and unforced, flowing from what's in your heart rather than from effort.

Influence in the back of the neck: the firmest part of the body, barely moved by anything. Your will stays steady, untouched by passing feelings. No regret, though you may influence fewer people this way.
Influence in the jaw, cheeks and tongue: it's only talk. Influence through words alone stays on the surface and moves nothing that matters. Let your actions carry what your words promise.
beneficial: Genuine, mutual attraction can grow into something lasting.
beware: Influence that is pushy, shallow, or one-sided won't hold.
reflections: What draws you to this?
How could you be more open here?
How mutual is the attraction?

label: Thunder over Wind
general: Endurance, constancy, commitment. Some things last not because they stay still but because they keep renewing themselves, like the seasons that change and yet continue. This hexagram follows Mutual Influence: after attraction comes the question of whether it can endure. Relationships, work, practices, promises: whatever lasts needs steady, ongoing effort and a clear sense of direction. Don't confuse duration with rigidity. Staying true doesn't mean never changing; it means changing in ways that keep the core intact. If you're committed to something, stay with it through the ordinary days, not just the exciting ones. That's how deep roots grow.
judgment: What lasts, not because it stands still but because it keeps moving in a steady rhythm. Commitment, constancy, the long haul. This brings success and no blame. Stay with what you've chosen, keep it alive by continuing to work at it, and it will carry you somewhere worth going.
image: Thunder and wind, always moving, always changing, yet always themselves. Be like that: hold your ground and keep your direction, even while the circumstances around you shift.
lineTexts: You want permanence too soon, digging deep before anything has been built. Expecting things to last before they've had time to grow leads nowhere. Persisting in this demand brings misfortune. Lasting things start light.

Regret disappears. Your strength is matched to the situation, balanced and not overreaching, and that moderation keeps you steady. This is how constancy actually works: not force, but the right measure, kept up over time.

You don't keep your character steady, and you lose your inner consistency. Others notice, and their trust falters. Persisting in this brings humiliation. Constancy means your values don't change with your mood.
No game in the field. You keep searching for something where it simply isn't, persisting in the wrong place. Endurance without the right direction is wasted effort. Look somewhere else.

You stay faithful to your role and keep your course. Tradition said this steadiness is fortunate in a wife and unfortunate in a husband, contrasting faithful following with active leading. Ask which your situation calls for: steady loyalty, or initiative and the courage to change.

Restlessness as a permanent state: always stirred up, always starting something new, never able to settle into anything long enough for it to take root. Change without a center can't last, and it wears out everyone around you. Misfortune.
beneficial: Steady commitment through ordinary days builds something that lasts.
beware: Constancy isn't rigidity; refusing to adapt will wear it down.
reflections: What would staying committed ask of you?
What needs to change so the core can last?
Where might steadiness be turning into stubbornness?

label: Heaven over Mountain
general: The tide is turning against you, and it's time to step back. Not in defeat or panic, but strategically, with dignity. Some situations can't be won by staying and fighting. Opposing forces are growing, and pushing against them now would only cost you. Retreating at the right moment protects your strength for later. This is wisdom, not cowardice. Keep a calm distance from what would drag you down: unhealthy dynamics, hostile people, pointless conflict. Do it without anger or contempt, so you don't get entangled even as you leave. Small progress is still possible. Just don't mistake this for a situation that calls for confrontation. Knowing when to withdraw is a form of strength.
judgment: A strategic withdrawal. The forces against you are rising, and this is not the time to fight them head-on. Pulling back now isn't defeat, it's wisdom, and it brings success. You can still make progress in small ways while you step aside from the larger struggle.
image: The mountain rises toward heaven, but heaven retreats beyond its reach. Keep your distance from what would drag you down, not with anger or contempt but with calm, dignified reserve.
lineTexts: You're the tail of the retreat, the last to leave, and that is the dangerous place. Don't try anything ambitious now. Stay quiet, make no sudden moves in any direction, and let the danger pass you by before you act.

You hold fast to your purpose as if bound with a strap of yellow oxhide, strong enough that nothing can break it. Even while others withdraw or waver, your commitment to what's right stays firm. That steadiness is your protection.

You want to step back, but something holds you: obligations, people who depend on you, ties you can't simply cut. That makes the retreat distressing and risky. Treat those who bind you with kindness and care, as you would people in your charge, and you can still come through well.

You step back even though part of you would rather stay. Leaving something you're fond of takes real strength of character. Done willingly and with a clear head, it brings good fortune. Someone ruled by their attachments couldn't manage it.
This is a retreat done well: timely, friendly, without bitterness or drama. You see the moment clearly and step away with grace. Stay steady and true in how you go, and it brings good fortune.

You withdraw cheerfully and completely, free of doubt and of anything left to hold you. This is retreat at its noblest: leaving with nothing owed and nothing regretted. Everything about it is favorable.
beneficial: Stepping back at the right moment preserves your strength.
beware: Staying to fight a battle you can't win will cost you dearly.
reflections: Which battle isn't worth fighting now?
How could you step back with dignity?
What would stepping back protect?

label: Thunder over Heaven
general: You have real power right now, energy, position, momentum, and it's rising. The temptation is to use all of it, to push hard because you can. But great strength carries great responsibility, and this hexagram asks you to be careful. Like a ram charging a fence and getting its horns caught, force without judgment gets stuck. True strength is knowing when to hold back, and making sure your power serves what's right. Ask whether what you want is fair, whether it serves others too, and whether you're acting from clarity or from ego. Strength that respects limits is hard to stop. Strength that ignores them often defeats itself.
judgment: Great strength, real power that is rising and ready to act. That much force is a gift and a test. The question isn't whether you can push through but whether you should. Stay steady and true, and make sure your strength serves what's right rather than just proving itself.
image: Thunder fills the sky, great power loud above the heavens. True strength knows its limits: don't take any path that cuts against what's fair and fitting, however strong you feel.
lineTexts: Your strength is all in your toes, eager to march before the rest of you is ready. Pushing forward from this low, early position will certainly go badly. Feel the power, but don't spend it yet.

Your strength is real and your position is balanced. Stay steady and true, and good fortune follows. The danger now isn't weakness but overconfidence: keep your power in measure and it will serve you well.

Someone small-minded would throw all their strength at this; someone wise knows not to. Forcing it now is like a ram butting a fence until its horns are caught. Even with good intentions, the position is risky. Hold back.

Persistence pays off: the fence gives way and the horns don't get caught. Regret disappears. Your strength now works like the axle of a heavy cart, steady and load-bearing rather than flashy. Quiet, consistent force gets you through.

You lose your ram-like stubbornness easily, almost without noticing, because the situation no longer calls for butting heads. There's no regret in letting it go. Not every moment needs a show of strength; some just need you to be at ease.

The ram has charged the fence and is stuck, unable to go forward or back. Nothing is gained by pushing harder. But if you recognize how difficult your position really is and stop struggling, things can still turn out well.
beneficial: Real power is rising; used rightly, it can achieve a great deal.
beware: Strength that ignores limits gets stuck, like a ram caught in a fence.
reflections: What is your strength for here?
Where might force get you stuck?
What would using your power fairly look like?

label: Fire over Earth
general: Progress, rapid and visible, like the sun rising over the earth. Things are going well. You may be gaining recognition, advancing in your work, or simply feeling your efforts pay off. This is a time of being seen and appreciated, and it brings genuine good fortune. Make the most of it, but stay true to yourself. The image asks you to let your own best qualities shine, not as self-promotion, but by becoming more fully who you are. Progress built on real merit lasts. If you find yourself chasing status for its own sake, pause. The sun rises because that's its nature, not because it's trying to impress anyone.
judgment: Easy, rapid progress, like the sun rising over the earth. You're being recognized and rewarded, welcomed and trusted. Things move forward smoothly now, and you can rise with them, as long as what drives you is genuinely good.
image: The sun rises above the earth and its light spreads in every direction. Let your own best qualities come out into the open the same way: clarify them, polish them, let them shine.
lineTexts: You want to move ahead, but something holds you back, and you may not be trusted yet. Stay true to your course anyway. If others don't believe in you, meet it with a generous, patient mind, and you'll make no mistake.

Your progress comes with a shadow of sadness, as if the advance doesn't feel the way you hoped. Stay steady and true. Help is coming from someone who cares about you, a kind, older presence the tradition calls the grandmother, and with it a great blessing.

The people around you trust you, and that trust carries you forward together. Whatever doubts or regrets you had fall away. Progress made with others' confidence is far stronger than progress made alone.

You're advancing like a hamster, a creature that hoards and scurries and hides. Gaining ground through grasping or hidden means puts you in danger, however correct you try to appear. Be open about what you're after, or don't pursue it.

Regret falls away. Don't fret over whether each step succeeds or fails; gains and losses matter less than the direction. Keep moving forward with good intentions, and the way ahead is favorable in every sense.

You're advancing with lowered horns, pushing hard, ready to fight. If you only use that force to set your own house in order, it can work, though the position is risky. But aggression remains aggression; even used for good, it leaves some cause for regret.
beneficial: Progress comes easily; your efforts are seen and appreciated.
beware: Chasing status for its own sake undermines the progress.
reflections: What progress are you making?
Which of your strengths could show more?
How much does recognition matter to you here?

label: Earth over Fire
general: Darkness has the upper hand. The light has sunk beneath the earth. You may be in a situation where good intentions are punished, where honesty isn't safe, or where someone in power is acting unjustly. The hexagram doesn't ask you to fight openly; that would only put you at greater risk. Instead, protect your inner light. Keep your values and your clarity intact, but don't make yourself a target. Be discreet. Endure. Many people have survived dark times by hiding their brightness without ever giving it up. Perseverance in adversity is the key. The night won't last forever, and your light will be needed when the dawn comes.
judgment: The light has gone into hiding. Something is wrong in the world around you, and it isn't safe to shine openly right now. Stay true inside even when the conditions are hard. Keep your light, but keep it veiled: hold steady through the dark rather than burning yourself out against it.
image: The light has sunk beneath the earth. When the times turn dark, live quietly among people, keep your clarity to yourself, and don't parade it. Your light is still there; it just doesn't need to be seen right now.
lineTexts: The light is wounded and you're flying with drooping wings. You may need to step away from a bad situation, even at real cost, going without comfort for a while. People may misunderstand or mock your choice. Leave anyway; staying would cost more.

You're wounded, but not fatally: hurt in the left thigh, as the old text puts it, an injury you can still move with. Use whatever strength you have left, like a swift horse, to get yourself and others to safety. There's good fortune in the rescue.

Hunting in the south, you come upon the source of the darkness and can confront it. But be careful: deep problems can't be fixed all at once. Even when you see clearly what's wrong, don't rush to set everything right in a single stroke.

You've come close enough to the darkness to understand it from the inside, to see what's really going on. With that understanding, you know you have to leave. Walk out through the gate and don't look back.

The tradition remembers the Prince of Ji, who lived at the court of a cruel king and survived by hiding his wisdom behind a show of madness. You may need to keep your light hidden in the same way, even very close to the harm. Stay true inside, and it is favorable.

There is no light at all, only darkness. What climbed to the top of the sky now falls into the earth. The power that darkens everything eventually destroys itself, because darkness can't sustain itself. Hold on; this is where the night ends.
beneficial: Your inner light survives dark times when you keep it safe.
beware: Shining openly now makes you a target; be discreet and endure.
reflections: What do you need to protect right now?
Where would it be wise to stay quiet?
What keeps you true to yourself in hard times?

label: Wind over Fire
general: The home, and the people you share it with. This hexagram is about the inner circle, family in any form, and about what holds it together: clear roles, mutual respect, and steadiness at the center. Each person knows their part and plays it faithfully. The traditional text placed this steadiness in the figure of the woman of the house; today it speaks to whoever keeps the home grounded. Order at home isn't about control. It's about consistency: words that match actions, and care that's reliable rather than dramatic. Influence spreads outward from here. If you want to change the world around you, start with how you live with those closest to you.
judgment: The home and the people in it, and the order that lets them live well together. A household holds when each person knows their place and plays it faithfully. Tradition pictured that steadiness at the heart of the home in the figure of the mother, whose care and constancy hold it together. Look after what's closest, and order spreads outward from there.
image: The wind rises out of the fire, warmth and influence moving outward from the hearth. Influence works the same way: make your words grounded in real things, and keep your conduct consistent over time.
lineTexts: Set clear ground rules at the very start. A home, a team, any close-knit group runs better when everyone knows the boundaries early, before habits harden and resentments form. Establish them now, kindly but clearly, and regret disappears.

In the traditional image, the woman at the center of the house doesn't chase her own ambitions but faithfully attends to the food. Read it for anyone: quiet, steady care for what nourishes others, given without seeking credit, brings good fortune.

When tempers flare at home, being too strict brings regret and risk, yet it still turns out better than being too lax. If everyone just laughs and does as they please, it ends in shame. Lean toward firmness, but stay warm.

You bring wealth and well-being into the home: not just money, but warmth, order and plenty. You look after what the household has and help it grow, wisely and fairly. This is a source of great good fortune for everyone under your roof.

The influence of whoever leads the household reaches everyone, not through fear but through love. There's no need to worry. When the people at the center are good, the whole family flourishes. Good fortune.

Your sincerity and the dignity of your character inspire respect. Lasting authority in any family or group comes from who you are, not from rules alone. Stay true, and in the end there is good fortune.
beneficial: Steadiness and consistency at home ripple outward into everything else.
beware: Words that don't match actions erode trust in your inner circle.
reflections: Who is closest to you in this?
Where do your words and actions not match?
What steadiness could you bring to your inner circle?

label: Fire over Lake
general: Things are pulling apart: two people, two ideas, two sides of yourself, moving in opposite directions like fire rising and water sinking. Big agreements aren't possible right now, and forcing them will only widen the gap. But that doesn't mean nothing can be done. Small things can still work out. Look for the common ground you do have, however limited. Accept that differences can be real and even valuable; opposites often clarify each other. The hexagram invites you to keep your own identity while still finding ways to relate. Harmony doesn't require sameness. Sometimes understanding comes from recognizing exactly where you differ.
judgment: Two forces pulling apart, like fire rising and water sinking. Agreement is hard now, so don't try to bring everything together at once. Small things can still go well. Work on what you can share, and accept the differences that remain.
image: Fire burns above, the lake lies below, each true to its own nature. Join with others where you can, but keep your own character intact; harmony doesn't require becoming the same.
lineTexts: Regret disappears. If you've lost your horses, don't chase them; they'll come back on their own. Likewise, if you meet people you disagree with, or who seem hostile, don't avoid them. Contact itself isn't the danger; forcing things is.

You meet the person you need in a narrow side lane rather than through the main gate: an unofficial, chance encounter. When the normal channels are closed, informal ones are fine. There's no fault in finding your way in through the side door.

Everything seems to go wrong at once: your cart is dragged back, your oxen are stopped, and you're humiliated by those around you. It's a bad beginning. But hold to the right connection, and despite the hard start, there will be a good end.

You feel isolated, alone in the middle of division. Then you meet someone of good faith, a kindred spirit, and you can trust each other fully. The situation is still risky, but with that bond you make no mistake.

Regret disappears. A true companion reaches out, and the connection comes as easily as biting through soft skin. You may have doubted you'd find anyone who understood you. With that ally by your side, go forward. What could go wrong?

Isolation has made you suspicious. You see a pig covered in mud, a cart full of demons, and you draw your bow. Then you look again and lower it: it isn't an enemy but someone who wants to join you. As the tension breaks, the rain falls and brings good fortune.
beneficial: Small agreements are still possible, and differences can clarify.
beware: Forcing big agreement now will only widen the gap.
reflections: Where exactly do you disagree?
What small agreement is still possible?
What about yourself do you want to keep?

label: Water over Mountain
general: You've run into an obstacle, a mountain ahead with dangerous water on top. Going straight at it won't work. The hexagram's advice may surprise you: stop, step back, and turn inward. Look at your own part in the difficulty. What could you change in yourself? This isn't blame; it's where your real power lies. At the same time, seek help. Find people who can support you, or someone wiser who can see what you can't. The old text points away from the mountains toward open, level ground: go where the way is easier rather than where it's hardest. Obstacles are often teachers. Work with this one patiently, and it will reshape you for the better.
judgment: The way ahead is blocked, like water stopped on a mountain path. Pushing forward into the obstruction leads nowhere. Instead, step back, find allies, and seek out someone wiser to guide you. Stay steady, and work around the problem rather than straight into it.
image: Water sits trapped on the mountain, unable to flow. When you're blocked, turn your attention inward: look honestly at your own part in the difficulty, and use the pause to grow.
lineTexts: Moving forward now leads into greater difficulty; waiting earns respect. You've only just met the obstacle, and you don't yet understand it. Stop, take in the situation, and let the right moment come, rather than walking straight into it.

You're struggling with obstacle after obstacle, but not for your own sake: you're carrying a responsibility to someone or something greater. No blame attaches to you here. Keep going, even when it's hard; the struggle itself is honorable.

Pressing ahead would only lead into deeper trouble, so you turn back toward the people who depend on you. That isn't defeat. They welcome your return, and your presence among them matters more right now than any advance.
Going forward leads into obstacles; staying lets you gather allies. This isn't the moment to push on alone. Join with those who can help, and together you'll be ready when the time comes.

You're in the middle of the greatest difficulty, and friends are coming to help you. Hold your place at the center and don't abandon your post. Your steadiness in the hardest moment is exactly what draws them to you.

Going on would only add to the obstacles; staying and helping brings great results. Turn back from your own escape, join those still in the thick of it, and seek out someone wise to guide the work. Good fortune follows.
beneficial: The obstacle is a chance to grow; help is there if you seek it.
beware: Charging straight at it leads nowhere; step back and look inward.
reflections: What part of this obstacle lies in you?
Who could help you see it differently?
What easier way around might you have missed?

label: Thunder over Water
general: The tension breaks. After a period of difficulty, the storm finally comes and clears the air, like thunder and rain after a heavy day. Something is loosening: a problem resolves, a burden lifts, a conflict ends. Now the question is what to do with the release. If there's nothing left to finish, return to ordinary life quickly; don't keep stirring up what's settled. If there's still something to do, do it promptly, then let it go. This is also a time for forgiveness: letting go of grudges, pardoning mistakes, releasing the past. Holding on to old tension would undo the relief. Move on lightly.
judgment: The knot comes loose. After a period of tension or danger, things begin to ease. If there's nothing more to be done, settle back into ordinary life quickly. If there is something left to finish, finish it promptly and then let it go.
image: Thunder and rain break the heaviness in the air, and everything breathes again. Bring that release to how you treat others: forgive mistakes, let go of old grievances, and don't drag the past forward.
lineTexts: The obstacle is gone, and there's no blame. Rest and recover. After a time of difficulty, sometimes the best thing to do is very little: let things settle, enjoy the quiet, and don't go looking for the next problem.
On the hunt, you catch three foxes and receive a golden arrow: you uncover hidden flatterers or false influences and remove them by honest means. Stay steady and true, and good fortune follows.

Someone carrying a porter's load rides in a fine carriage, looking like more than they are, and robbers notice. Pretending to a position you haven't earned invites trouble. However correct you try to be, it ends in regret. Be honest about where you stand.

Free yourself from those who cling to you, the way you'd shake off something dragging at your feet. Once you do, true friends come: people you can trust, and who can trust you. Let go of the wrong ties to make room for the right ones.

Only you can release yourself from what holds you back. Do it, firmly and with integrity, and good fortune follows. Even people of lesser character will see that you mean it, and they'll fall away or change.

The prince shoots a hawk perched high on a wall, and hits it. A stubborn obstacle, set high and out of reach, can be removed with the right aim and the right timing. Prepare well, act once, and everything becomes favorable.
beneficial: Tension is easing; forgive, release, and move on lightly.
beware: Clinging to old grievances will undo the relief.
reflections: What tension is finally easing?
What still needs finishing?
Which grudge could you let go of?

label: Mountain over Lake
general: Something has to be reduced: cut back, simplified, given up. That can feel like loss, but the hexagram sees it differently. Decrease, done sincerely, brings great good fortune. Sometimes less really is more: fewer commitments, less noise, simpler habits, holding back anger or desire. The old text says even a modest offering is enough, if it's honest. This also works between people: giving something up so that someone else can grow, like the lake at the foot of the mountain whose water feeds the green slopes above. Ask what you could let go of that would make room for something better. The point isn't to deprive yourself, but to put your resources where they truly matter.
judgment: Less, given willingly. Something has to be cut back, simplified, or offered up, and if you do it sincerely, it brings great good fortune. The form doesn't need to be grand: even a small, honest offering is enough. What matters is the spirit behind it.
image: The lake lies at the foot of the mountain, giving up its water so the heights can be green. Reduce what needs reducing in yourself: hold back anger, rein in impulses, and trust that what you give up feeds something higher.
lineTexts: You drop your own affairs to rush and help someone else. That's generous and blameless. But think about how much you can really give without draining yourself. Help that leaves you empty can't last.

Stay true and steady; rushing into action would go badly. You can help others without diminishing yourself, and without giving up your own dignity to please them. Sometimes the greatest gift you can offer is simply staying who you are.

When three travel together, one is lost; when one travels alone, they find a companion. Closeness works best in twos. A crowd breeds jealousy and division, while someone on their own finds the partner they need.

Lessening your faults, old wounds and bad habits brings others gladly to your side. When you let go of what's holding you back, help arrives quickly, and people are glad to give it. There's no blame in it, only relief.

Help arrives from beyond what you sought, worth as much as ten pairs of precious tortoise shells, and nothing can turn it away. Supreme good fortune. When you've given up what wasn't needed, abundance finds its way to you.

You can increase others without taking anything from yourself. No blame. Stay steady and true, and good fortune follows. Whatever you undertake goes well, and you'll have the support of more people than you could ever count.
beneficial: Letting go sincerely makes room for something better.
beware: Cut back wisely; decrease for its own sake is just loss.
reflections: What could you simplify or let go?
What would letting go make room for?
What small, honest gift could you give?

label: Wind over Thunder
general: Gain is coming. Resources, support, opportunity, energy: things are flowing in, and it's a good time to act boldly, to start something or take a leap. Increase like this doesn't last forever, so use it while it's here. But the hexagram is clear about the spirit of it: true increase comes when those above give to those below, when abundance is shared. Use your good fortune to help others grow too. The image of wind and thunder strengthening each other also points inward: when you see something good in others, adopt it; when you see a fault in yourself, let it go. Increase isn't just accumulation. It's growth.
judgment: More, flowing in. A time of gain and expansion, when help comes from above and things grow. It's good to undertake something now, even something ambitious. Use the increase well: let it reach others and not just yourself.
image: Wind and thunder feed each other, each making the other stronger. Grow the same way: when you see something good, take it on; when you see a fault in yourself, let it go.
lineTexts: With the support you're receiving, now is the time to attempt something great, something you couldn't manage alone. If it turns out well, no one will blame you for the boldness. Use the gift fully, and make sure it serves more than yourself.

Help and blessings come from beyond you, worth ten pairs of precious tortoise shells, and nothing can turn them away. Stay steady and true. Offer your gratitude, the way a king once made offerings to heaven, and good fortune follows.

Even misfortune brings increase here: hard experiences can teach and strengthen you. There's no blame if you stay sincere and keep to the middle path. Present yourself honestly, as an official once came before the prince bearing the token of his rank.

Keeping to the middle path, you become the trusted go-between, the one whose counsel is followed. You could even be relied on for something as large as moving a capital. Use that trust to benefit everyone, not just yourself.

Your kindness is sincere, and you don't ask whether it will be rewarded. There's no need to ask. Supreme good fortune. People recognize true goodness and return it, and your generosity comes back to you.

You seek only your own gain and help no one. No one helps you either, and some will move against you. When the heart has no steady principle, things turn bad. Increase without generosity leads to misfortune.
beneficial: Gain is flowing in; a good time for bold undertakings.
beware: Increase that isn't shared or used for growth won't last.
reflections: What is growing for you right now?
Who could you share it with?
Which good habit could you take on?

label: Lake over Heaven
general: It's time for a breakthrough. Something that has been building up must now be resolved: a problem, a harmful influence, a pattern that can't continue. The hexagram shows five strong lines pushing out the last weak one at the top. You're in a position to act, but how you act matters. Be open and honest about it: name the problem truthfully, even if that carries some risk. Don't use force, revenge, or underhanded methods; fighting dirty would make you part of the problem. Be resolute, but stay fair. And once it's done, don't cling to your victory. Like a lake rising to heaven and returning as rain, share what you've gained.
judgment: A breakthrough. Something that has built up must now be resolved, decisively and in the open. Name it honestly, even if that carries some risk, and let the people closest to you know where you stand. Don't fight dirty or force it with violence; act with clarity and the way will open.
image: The lake has risen up to heaven, and the water must eventually come down as rain. Share what you've accumulated rather than hoarding it, and don't rest on the good you've already done.
lineTexts: Your strength is in your toes, eager to march before you're ready. Going ahead now won't succeed, and the failure will count against you. A breakthrough needs more than impulse; it needs you to know your own strength before you test it.
Stay alert, keep sounding the warning, and keep your guard up. Even if danger comes in the middle of the night, you won't need to fear it. Being prepared takes the sting out of surprise.

Showing your determination too openly brings misfortune. Yet someone resolved to deal with the problem may have to walk alone through the rain, even if others suspect them of siding with the wrong party. It stings, but in the end there's no blame.

There's no skin on your thighs and you walk with difficulty: restless, uncomfortable, unable to settle. If you could let yourself be led like a sheep, following rather than pushing, regret would disappear. But you may hear this advice and not believe it.

Weeds like purslane grow back however often you pull them; half measures won't do. Deal with this problem with full, steady resolve, from the center, without going to extremes or losing your balance. Then there is no blame.
No one to call on, no help in sight. What refused to be removed finally falls, and the end is misfortune. If you're holding on to something that has to go, don't wait until there's no choice left.
beneficial: Resolute, honest action can clear away what has to go.
beware: Force, revenge, or underhanded methods will make you part of the problem.
reflections: What has to be settled now?
How could you say it openly and fairly?
Once it's resolved, what will you let go of?

label: Heaven over Wind
general: Something unexpected comes to meet you: a person, an idea, a temptation, an opportunity. It may seem small, but it carries real force. The hexagram shows a single yielding line slipping in below five strong ones, a small influence that can grow quickly if left unchecked. The old text warns against binding yourself to it. Not because encounters are bad, they're how life moves, but because what enters easily can quietly take over. Engage if you must, but stay aware, and don't hand over control. Keep things in the open. Influence is healthiest when it's clear and visible, not hidden in the gaps where it can grow unseen.
judgment: Something unexpected comes to meet you, small and modest-looking but stronger than it seems. Notice its pull. The old text warns against binding yourself to it: what arrives easily can quietly take over. Engage with it if you must, but don't hand it control.
image: Wind moves beneath the whole sky, reaching every corner. Let your influence travel like that: clearly, openly, and to everyone it concerns, so nothing grows unseen in the gaps.
lineTexts: Stop the problem while it's small. Fasten it to a strong brake, the way you'd chock the wheel of a cart. Let it wander and misfortune follows, like a lean, restless pig that runs wild the moment it's loose. Check what's creeping in early.
The fish is in your basket: the troublesome influence is contained, under your watch. No blame. But don't let it out among the guests. Keep it where you can see it, rather than letting it spread.

Restless and uncomfortable, you can't settle into the situation, as if the skin had been stripped from your thighs. It's risky, but you aren't making a great mistake. Your discomfort is keeping you from getting too entangled.
There's no fish in your basket: you've lost touch with the people you depend on, or who depend on you. Holding yourself aloof brings misfortune. Don't neglect those around you; you'll need them.

Like a tall willow sheltering a melon, you protect what's growing beneath you without forcing it. Keep your brilliance to yourself and let your quality work quietly. What's meant to come will drop from heaven in its own time.

You meet others with your horns: proud, aloof, withdrawn. That keeps you clean but cuts you off, and there's regret in it. Still, there's no blame. Sometimes keeping your distance is the price of integrity.
beneficial: An unexpected encounter can bring new energy and possibilities.
beware: What enters easily can quietly take over; don't hand it control.
reflections: What has come into your life unexpectedly?
What small thing might be gaining too much influence?
How can you stay in charge of your choices?

label: Lake over Earth
general: People are gathering, around a cause, a leader, a celebration, a shared purpose. This hexagram brings success, but it asks what holds the gathering together. Groups need a center: good leadership, shared values, something larger than individual interests. The old image is the king at the ancestral temple, uniting people through something sacred they hold in common. Generous contribution pays off now; it's a good time to commit and work together. But wherever many people gather, conflict and the unexpected can arise too. Stay prepared and keep your eyes open, and you'll be able to handle trouble calmly if it comes.
judgment: A gathering. People come together around a shared center, and this brings success. It needs leadership worth trusting and a sense of something larger than any one person. Generous effort pays off now; it's a good time to commit and move forward together.
image: The lake rises over the earth, water collecting wherever it can. Where people gather, so does the unexpected: stay prepared, so you can meet trouble calmly if it comes.
lineTexts: You want to come together with others, but your sincerity wavers and things fall into confusion. Call out for help. A single handshake can turn tears into laughter. Don't worry; moving forward brings no blame.

Let yourself be drawn in, guided toward the people you belong with. Good fortune, and no blame. When you are sincere, even a small offering is enough. You don't need to make a great show of belonging; it comes from the heart.

You want to join the gathering, but you're left sighing on the outside, finding no place. Go forward anyway. There may be some small embarrassment, but no real blame. A connection is worth seeking, even if it's awkward.

You gather people for the sake of something greater, not for yourself. Great good fortune and no blame, as long as you're truly working for something beyond your own interest. Check your motives honestly; the gathering is only as good as its purpose.

You stand at the center of the gathering, and that brings no blame. But if some don't trust you yet, it's your character, not your position, that will win them. Be steady, enduring and true, and regret disappears.

Sighing and weeping, you feel shut out of the circle, or misunderstood by those you hoped to join. That grief shows you understand what's been lost, and there's no blame in it. Sincere longing, honestly expressed, can still lead you back.
beneficial: Gathering around a shared purpose brings success.
beware: Where people gather, trouble can arise; stay prepared.
reflections: What brings people together here?
What could you contribute?
What trouble would be worth preparing for?

label: Earth over Wind
general: Steady upward growth, like a tree rising from the earth: slowly, naturally, one ring at a time. This isn't explosive success; it's the kind that comes from consistent effort in the right direction, and it brings great good fortune. It's a good time to seek out people who can help you, and not to be held back by fear. Move toward what you want. The key is patience and persistence: small steps, added together, become something high and great. Don't try to skip stages. Trust the growth that's already underway, and keep going.
judgment: Rising, steadily, like a young tree growing upward through the soil. This brings great success. Seek out people who can help you, and don't be afraid to move toward what you want. Effort now carries you forward, one natural stage at a time.
image: Within the earth, the wood keeps growing. Grow the same way: through devoted, patient steps, adding small things to small things until they build into something high.
lineTexts: Your rise begins, and you're welcomed by those above you. Great good fortune. Like a young shoot that has found good soil and open sky, you're rooted from below and trusted from above. Start your climb with confidence; the ground is solid.

When you're sincere, even a simple, modest offering is enough, like the small spring sacrifice the old text mentions. You don't need a grand gesture or an impressive display to be accepted. No blame. Let your honesty speak for you.

You rise into an empty city: no resistance, no one in the way. Everything opens before you, almost too easily. Enjoy the ease and make use of it, but stay alert. Growth this smooth is rare, and an empty city can also mean no one is there to help.
The king makes offerings on Mount Qi, and you are trusted to take part. You're rising into a place of real responsibility and respect. Good fortune, and no mistake. Honor the trust you've been given.

Stay steady and true, and good fortune follows. You climb step by step, one stair after another, with the care of someone ascending a ceremonial staircase. There's no shortcut, and no need for one. Each step taken properly carries you higher than a leap would.

You keep pushing upward in the dark, not knowing where you're going, climbing for the sake of climbing. Blind ambition won't take you far. What helps now is steady, constant effort, keeping your integrity as you climb and knowing why you climb.
beneficial: Steady upward growth; keep going and seek good help.
beware: Trying to skip stages will undermine the growth.
reflections: What is growing step by step?
Whose help could you ask for?
Which step are you tempted to skip?

label: Lake over Water
general: You're worn out, pressed in from all sides, out of resources. The lake has drained; there's no water left. You may feel trapped, unheard, or misunderstood: when you speak, no one believes you. This is a genuinely hard place. But the hexagram also says it can lead to success, if you stay true to yourself. Hardship tests what you're made of, and it can deepen you in ways ease never would. Don't waste words trying to convince people right now; let your actions speak. Hold on to what you value most. Even when everything else is taken away, your inner commitment remains, and that is what carries you through.
judgment: Exhausted, pressed in, drained. The resources have run out and your words aren't being believed. This is a hard place, but not a hopeless one. If you stay true to yourself, you can come through it and even grow. Let what you do speak for you, since what you say won't be heard right now.
image: The lake has emptied; the water has drained away below it. When everything around you runs dry, stake yourself on what you truly value. That is the one thing hardship can't take.
lineTexts: You sit beneath a bare tree with nothing to shelter you, and wander into a dark valley. For three years you see no way out. This is the low point, and part of the darkness is your own discouragement. Don't let despair become your home.

You're surrounded by food and wine and still oppressed: comfortable on the outside, empty within. Help is on its way from someone in a position to give it. Stay sincere, as if in prayer. Pushing forward now would go badly, but you are not to blame.

You beat against a rock and lean on thorns. You go home and your partner isn't there. Clinging to what hurts you, or to what can't hold you, leads to misfortune. See what won't support you, and stop leaning on it.
You come slowly, held back by a golden carriage: the power and wealth that surround you. It's humbling, but in the end it turns out well. Even if you're late, keep going toward those who need you.

Your nose and feet are cut off: you're pressed from above and below, blocked by those in power. But slowly, relief comes. Stay sincere, as if making an offering, and things gradually ease. Patience and faith carry you through.

You're tangled in vines, teetering on an unsteady perch, telling yourself any move will bring regret. But by now the oppression is mostly in your mind. Recognize that, regret your past mistakes, and move forward. Good fortune comes.
beneficial: Hardship can deepen you; your inner commitment can't be taken away.
beware: Words won't convince anyone now; let your actions speak instead.
reflections: What has run out, and what is left?
Where could actions speak louder than words?
What can't hardship take from you?

label: Water over Wind
general: The well: a source of nourishment that stays the same while everything around it changes. People come and go, towns are rebuilt, but the well remains, neither drying up nor overflowing. This hexagram asks about your deepest resources, what truly sustains you and others: wisdom, community, inner life, the shared foundations of being human. These don't run out. But they have to be tended. If the rope is too short or the bucket is broken, the water can't reach you. Ask what's blocking your access to what nourishes you, and what might need repair. Then share what you draw. A well only matters when people drink from it.
judgment: The well, a source that doesn't change even when everything around it does. Towns are rebuilt and people come and go, but the well stays where it is, never running out, never overflowing. The danger is not the source but the drawing: if the rope is too short or the bucket breaks, the water can't reach you. Tend to how you draw on what nourishes you.
image: Water rises through the wood, the way a well's bucket lifts water to the surface. Help the people around you draw on what sustains them, and encourage them to help each other.
lineTexts: No one drinks from a muddy well, and no creatures come to an old one. If you let yourself go to waste, neglected and unused, you'll have nothing to offer. Tend the source before you expect anyone to drink.

Water leaks from the well through a hole, trickling down to the small fish below, or seeps out of a broken jar. Your gifts are being spent on small things, or wasted entirely. Repair what's broken and use what you have well.

The well has been cleaned, but no one drinks from it. That's a shame, because the water is good. If only someone in charge recognized it, everyone would benefit. Your worth may go unseen for now. Don't let it spoil.
The well is being relined. While you repair and strengthen yourself, you can't give water to others, and that's fine. No blame. The inner work you do now prepares you to serve later.

The well is clear, a cold, fresh spring that everyone drinks from. Your gifts are pure, and they're finally being used and valued. This is the source at its best: what you have to give and what others need have met.

The water is drawn up and the well is left uncovered, open to anyone who comes. Nothing is held back or rationed. This is generosity at its fullest: reliable, dependable and freely shared. Great good fortune.
beneficial: Your deepest resources don't run out; draw on them and share them.
beware: A broken rope means no water; tend how you reach what sustains you.
reflections: What truly nourishes you here?
What is getting in the way of it?
Who could you share it with?

label: Lake over Fire
general: Deep change is coming, the turning of an era, the shedding of an old skin. Something in your life has run its course and needs to be replaced. Change of this size can't be rushed. It needs the right timing, and it needs the trust of those it affects. When the moment truly arrives, act with conviction and clear purpose. Explain the change and make the new order understandable, the way a calendar makes the seasons clear. Done this way, regret disappears and the transformation succeeds. Change for its own sake, or change forced too early, only causes chaos. Ask whether the time is really ripe.
judgment: The old falls away and something new must take its place. A change this deep is only trusted once its moment has truly arrived. When it has, act with conviction, and keep your purpose clean. Then the change succeeds and regret disappears.
image: Fire in the lake, two forces that cannot stay as they are. When transformation comes, give it a clear rhythm, the way a calendar marks the seasons, so people can understand the change they're living through.
lineTexts: Too early to change anything yet. The old image is being bound in the hide of a yellow ox, held firm by something tough and steady. Stay put and stay grounded for now. The case for change is still forming, and acting before it's ready would only cut you loose from the support you'll need later.

Now the time has come. You've waited, watched the situation ripen, and the change you've been considering is ready to be made. Act. Moving now brings good fortune, and there's nothing to reproach in it. Change made after due patience carries a weight that hasty change never has.

Pushing ahead blindly here leads to trouble, even if your cause is right. The position is precarious. Talk the change through, carefully and more than once, until people genuinely understand it. When it has been weighed three times over, you'll be believed, and only then can it go forward.

Doubt and regret fall away. People trust you now, and that trust is what makes deep change possible. Even reshaping long-standing rules brings good fortune when it rests on real confidence. The change isn't imposed from outside; it's carried by belief in what you're doing.

The old image is the tiger changing its stripes: a transformation so clear and striking that everyone can see it. You don't need to consult anyone or ask for signs. People already trust you, before you've even begun. When change comes from someone this grounded, it is bold, visible and right.

The change is done. The old image is the leopard changing its spots, a finer and subtler shift, while those who resisted now change their faces and go along. Don't push for more. Further upheaval would bring misfortune. Settle into the new order, steady and true, and let it take root.
beneficial: The time for real change has come; act with conviction and clarity.
beware: Change forced too early, or without trust, only causes chaos.
reflections: What has run its course?
How will you know the time is right?
How could you help others understand the change?

label: Fire over Wind
general: The cauldron: a vessel for cooking, for turning raw things into nourishment, and in ancient China a sacred symbol of a well-founded order. After the upheaval of change comes the work of building something new and stable, and this hexagram brings great good fortune to that work. What you establish now can hold and feed many people, if it's built on the right foundation. Take your proper place in it. Be steady and responsible. Pay attention to what goes into the vessel: values, intentions, the quality of what you offer. A good cauldron transforms ordinary ingredients into something that sustains life. That's the kind of work this moment calls for.
judgment: The cauldron, a vessel for transforming raw things into nourishment, and a symbol of something new taking its rightful form. This is a time of great good fortune and success. What you build now can hold and feed many people, if it's built on the right foundation.
image: Fire burns above the wood that feeds it, cooking in the cauldron what will feed people. Take your rightful place and hold it steady, so what you're meant to do can come to fullness.
lineTexts: The cauldron is turned upside down, feet in the air, and that's not all bad. Tipping it out clears away the stale old contents. The old text adds an image of someone in a lowly place who is raised up through a child: an unconventional route to good standing. Clearing out what's spoiled is no mistake here.

The cauldron is full; there's real substance in what you hold. Others may envy you or wish you harm, but they can't reach you while you stay focused on your purpose. Keep your attention on the work and not on them. That steadiness brings good fortune.

The cauldron's handles are damaged, so it can't be lifted and the rich food inside goes uneaten. Your gifts aren't being recognized or used right now, and that's frustrating. Stay patient and keep refining what you offer. The rain will come, the frustration will ease, and in the end there is good fortune.

The cauldron's legs break and the prince's meal spills out. You've taken on more than you can carry, or trusted the wrong people to help, and now it shows. It's an embarrassing failure and it brings misfortune. Learn the lesson: match your commitments to your real strength.

The cauldron has golden handles and carrying rings of bronze: it can be lifted and used, and it serves well. You're open to good counsel, receptive and steady at the center, and so the right help reaches you. Hold to what is right and this brings advantage.

Now the cauldron has rings of jade, hard yet gentle, precious yet plain. Strength and softness are in balance, and what you've built can feed everyone. This is great good fortune, and everything you undertake from here goes well.
beneficial: What you build now can nourish many, if the foundation is right.
beware: Mind what goes into the vessel; poor ingredients spoil the whole.
reflections: What are you building?
What are you putting into it?
Who could it eventually feed?

label: Thunder over Thunder
general: A shock, thunder that makes everyone jump. Something sudden has happened or is about to: a surprise, a jolt, a disruption that shakes things up. The first reaction is fear. But the hexagram says this can bring success. Shock wakes you up. It forces you to pay attention, to examine your life, to put things in order. The old text describes someone so steady that even thunder rolling across a hundred miles doesn't make them drop the sacred cup they're holding. That's the challenge: let the shock move you without losing your center. Afterward there may even be laughter, the relief of having come through. Use the jolt as a call to act.
judgment: A shock, like a thunderclap that makes everyone jump. Fear comes first, then relief, even laughter. The shock reaches far, but someone steady in themselves doesn't drop what they're holding. Let the jolt wake you up rather than knock you over, and it brings success.
image: Thunder comes again and again. Let it shake you into attention: look at your own life honestly, set it in order, and use the fear as a chance to grow.
lineTexts: The thunder comes and you start in fear, looking around for danger. Then the shock passes, and you find yourself laughing and talking again. That's the right sequence: let the fear wake you up, then let it go. Having been shaken teaches caution, and that brings good fortune.

The shock puts you in real danger, and you may lose something of value. Don't chase after it. Climb to higher ground, out of harm's way. Let go of what you can't hold on to right now. In seven days, the old text says, it comes back to you without your having to pursue it.

The shock leaves you dazed and unsteady. But if you let it move you to act, to change what needs changing, it does no harm. Being shaken can be the push you needed. Don't freeze; use the jolt as a call to correct your course.

Shock leaves you stuck, sinking deeper into the mud. Instead of waking you, the jolt has bogged you down, and nothing moves. This is a warning: when the shock comes and you can't respond, don't wallow. Find one small solid step and take it, before you sink further.

Shocks keep coming, back and forth, and danger is all around. But if you keep your center and stay focused on what really matters, you lose nothing essential. There is still work you can do even amid the commotion. Steadiness in motion is the gift of this line.

Shock grips you completely; you're trembling and looking around wildly. Acting now, in this state, would bring misfortune. Pull back before the danger reaches you, and take precautions while it's still with others. People close to you may grumble about your caution. Let them. It keeps you free of blame.
beneficial: The shock wakes you up and gives you a chance to set things in order.
beware: Don't let fear knock you off your center.
reflections: What shook you?
What is it waking you up to?
What helps you stay calm through it?

label: Mountain over Mountain
general: Stop. Be still, like a mountain: unmoving, grounded. This hexagram is about stillness, not as inactivity but as presence, quieting the restless body and mind so you can see clearly. Sometimes the most important thing you can do is nothing at all. Step back from the noise, from the pull of other people's demands, even from your own racing thoughts. The old text speaks of keeping the back still, the part of you that you can't see, a calm deeper than willpower. In that quiet, you make no mistakes. Keep your thoughts on the present situation, not running ahead. When the time comes to move again, you'll move from a place of calm.
judgment: Stillness, the mountain at rest. Stop. Quiet the body, quiet the restless mind, and step back from the noise of the moment, even from the people around you. This isn't withdrawal from life but a return to center. In that stillness, you make no mistakes.
image: Mountains stand side by side, each unmoving. Keep your thoughts where you are: don't let your mind race ahead or wander beyond what the moment actually asks of you.
lineTexts: Keeping your toes still, before you've even taken a step. Stopping right at the start, before you've committed to a course, is wise and costs nothing. It's easy to stay still when you've barely moved. Hold to that steadiness consistently, and it keeps you clear of mistakes.

Keeping your calves still, while the body above keeps moving. You're carried along by someone else's momentum and can't stop it, though you sense it's wrong. You can't rescue the situation, and your heart isn't at peace with it. Notice the discomfort; it's telling you something true.

Keeping your hips still, so stiffly that the body is split in two. Stillness forced on yourself through rigidity isn't real calm. It's suppression, and the pressure smolders inside. This is dangerous. True stillness can't be won by clenching; it comes from letting the restlessness settle on its own.

Keeping your trunk still, the center of the body at rest. You're not yet beyond your own impulses, but you're learning to quiet yourself where it matters most. No mistake in that. It's real progress, even if full stillness isn't here yet.

Keeping your jaws still: your words become ordered and measured. When you don't let your mouth run ahead of you, what you say carries weight and regret falls away. Speak less, and only when it's needed, and your words will land.

Stillness that has become generous and settled, the calm of someone who has truly found their center. You aren't forcing it anymore; it's simply who you are. This is good fortune, and the deepest form of keeping still.
beneficial: Stillness brings clarity; in quiet you make no mistakes.
beware: Racing thoughts and restless action will cloud your judgment now.
reflections: What would happen if you paused?
Which thoughts are racing ahead of you?
What do you see from a calmer place?

label: Wind over Mountain
general: Slow growth, step by step, in the right order. Like a tree on a mountainside, growing slowly but surely, rooted and visible. Or like a marriage in the old tradition, which unfolded through its proper stages rather than all at once. Things that last are built gradually. Don't rush this. Every stage has its purpose, and skipping ahead would weaken the whole. Patience and perseverance bring good fortune. This applies to influence too: you change the people around you not through sudden pressure, but through steady goodness over time. Let it develop at its own pace.
judgment: Slow, steady development, the way a tree grows on a mountain, or the way a lasting union unfolds through its proper stages. Rushing would ruin it. Let things progress one step at a time, and they come to good fortune. Patience and perseverance carry it.
image: A tree grows on the mountain, rooted and visible to all. Influence builds slowly too: steady goodness, practiced over time, quietly lifts the people around you.
lineTexts: The wild goose draws near the shore, the first cautious step of a long journey. You're young in this, inexperienced and exposed, and some may criticize you. That's no mistake. Small, careful steps at the beginning are exactly right; the criticism will pass as you find your footing.

The goose reaches the large rock, a safe place where it can eat and drink in peace. You've found a secure footing and can enjoy what it offers. Share it freely. This is good fortune: a stage reached gently, after patient progress.

The goose reaches the dry plateau, too far from water, out of its element. The old image is of a household broken: a husband who leaves and doesn't come back, a child who can't be raised. Pushing on recklessly brings misfortune. What helps now is guarding what you have, not venturing further.

The goose reaches a tree. It's not built for perching, but it may find a flat branch to rest on. You're somewhere that isn't quite right for you, and that's no mistake if you're flexible. Find whatever safe footing is available, and stay humble while you're there.

The goose reaches the summit. The old image is of a couple long kept apart by misunderstanding or by others, without children for three years. But in the end, nothing can prevent what's meant to come together. Patience is rewarded, and there is good fortune.

The goose flies beyond the heights, into open sky, and its feathers can be used in sacred dances. You've grown past the ordinary stages, and your example now serves others. That's good fortune: the long, gradual journey has become something others can learn from.
beneficial: Slow, steady progress through proper stages leads to lasting results.
beware: Rushing ahead will weaken the whole.
reflections: What stage is this really at?
What are you trying to rush?
What steady effort could make a difference over time?

label: Thunder over Lake
general: You're in a situation you didn't fully choose, from a position of limited power. The old image is a young woman married into a household as a secondary wife: her place is set, and she can't simply change it. Pushing forward, trying to take control, or acting as though you have more power than you do would bring misfortune. That doesn't mean you have no agency. It means acting wisely within your circumstances: seeing them clearly, keeping your dignity, and understanding the arrangement in light of the longer story. Ask what's truly lasting here, and what is only temporary. Build on what lasts.
judgment: A situation you didn't fully choose, entered from a lesser position, like a young woman married into a household where she has little say. Pushing forward or trying to take control here brings misfortune. See the arrangement for what it is, and act within it wisely rather than against it.
image: Thunder over the lake, sudden stirring over still water. See what is passing in light of what lasts: understand where things are likely to end, so you don't build on what is only temporary.
lineTexts: The traditional image is a younger sister married into the household as a secondary wife, with little say over her place. In any situation where you hold a lesser role, you can still do real good, like someone with a limp who still walks. Moving forward, quietly and within your role, brings good fortune.

In the old image she is blind in one eye and still able to see: limited, but not helpless. Your circumstances may disappoint you, or someone you depend on may fall short. Stay loyal to your own values in private, the way a person living alone keeps their integrity intact. That advantage remains yours.

The old image shows someone waiting to marry who accepts a lower position to get there. Rushing into an arrangement beneath you, just to have something, may not hold. Taking the lesser place out of impatience is a step back. Ask yourself whether waiting for something more fitting would be wiser.

In the traditional image, the marriage is delayed past the usual time. Holding out for the right arrangement, rather than settling for whatever comes first, is worth it. Your time will come. Patience here isn't missing out; it's choosing well.

The traditional image is a princess married in plain clothes, her sleeves less fine than her attendant's. Someone in a high place who doesn't need outward display has real dignity. Like the moon nearly full, this humility shines without needing to show itself. Good fortune.

The ritual is empty: a basket with nothing in it, a sacrifice with no blood. The form of the commitment is there, but no substance. A bond kept up only for appearances can't carry anything. Nothing here is favorable; look honestly at whether this arrangement holds anything real.
beneficial: Seeing your situation clearly lets you act wisely within it.
beware: Overreaching or forcing control from a weak position brings misfortune.
reflections: What here didn't you choose?
How can you act wisely within your limits?
What here will last, and what won't?

label: Thunder over Fire
general: Fullness, a peak moment of abundance, power, and achievement, like the sun at noon.
